// Unobserved dump records — universal clean-up of self-modifying-bytecode leftovers in residual programs.
//
// After specialisation the residual code may still write into the dump's records (the patches the original
// bytecode applied to itself) and test them in one-time guards:
//
//   if K_16[2092] == 2760 then else K_16[2092] = 2760; K_12[7] = 1 end
//   K_16[1684] = 2403
//
// A record that the residual program only ever writes at literal keys, or tests in such guards (an if whose
// branches do nothing but write records of the same kind), can no longer influence the program: its stores
// and guards are removed. A record read anywhere else (a run-time selected variant, an alias, a call
// argument) keeps all of its stores, and so do the records written under a guard on it (fixpoint).
import type * as A from '../ast.js';
import { analyzeScopes } from '../analysis/scope.js';

export interface RecordCleanResult { stores: number; guards: number; records: number; changed: Set<string>; notes: string[]; }

const unparen = (e: A.Expr): A.Expr => { while (e && e.type === 'ParenExpr') e = e.expr; return e; };
const isLit = (e: A.Expr | undefined): boolean => {
  if (!e) return false; const u = unparen(e);
  if (u.type === 'NumberLit' || u.type === 'StringLit' || u.type === 'TrueLit' || u.type === 'FalseLit' || u.type === 'NilLit') return true;
  return u.type === 'UnExpr' && u.op === '-' && unparen(u.expr).type === 'NumberLit';
};

export function dropUnobservedRecords(protos: Array<{ id: string; chunk: A.Chunk }>, recordId: (name: string) => string | null): RecordCleanResult {
  const res: RecordCleanResult = { stores: 0, guards: 0, records: 0, changed: new Set(), notes: [] };
  interface Store { proto: string; stmt: A.AssignStat; rec: string; }
  interface Guard { proto: string; stmt: A.IfStat; rec: string; stores: Store[]; }
  const stores: Store[] = [];
  const guards: Guard[] = [];
  const observed = new Set<string>();
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  const storeOf = new Map<A.Stat, Store>();
  for (const p of protos) {
    const sc = analyzeScopes(p.chunk);
    const recOf = (e: A.Expr | undefined): string | null => {
      const u = e && unparen(e);
      if (!u || u.type !== 'NameExpr') return null;
      const b = sc.refOf.get(u);
      if (b && b.kind !== 'global') return null;
      return recordId(u.name);
    };
    // the record store `REC[lit] = lit`
    const asStore = (s: A.Stat): string | null => {
      if (s.type !== 'AssignStat' || s.op || s.targets.length !== 1 || s.values.length !== 1) return null;
      const t = unparen(s.targets[0]);
      if (t.type !== 'IndexExpr' || !isLit(t.index) || !isLit(s.values[0])) return null;
      return recOf(t.obj);
    };
    // the guard condition `REC[lit] == lit` (or ~=, or not (…))
    const guardRec = (c: A.Expr): string | null => {
      let u = unparen(c);
      if (u.type === 'UnExpr' && u.op === 'not') u = unparen(u.expr);
      if (u.type !== 'BinExpr' || (u.op !== '==' && u.op !== '~=')) return null;
      const side = (a: A.Expr, b: A.Expr) => { const ua = unparen(a); return ua.type === 'IndexExpr' && isLit(ua.index) && isLit(b) ? recOf(ua.obj) : null; };
      return side(u.left, u.right) ?? side(u.right, u.left);
    };
    const counted = new Set<A.NameExpr>();
    const visitStmts = (list: A.Stat[]) => {
      for (const s of list) {
        const r = asStore(s);
        if (r !== null) { const st = { proto: p.id, stmt: s as A.AssignStat, rec: r }; stores.push(st); storeOf.set(s, st); seen.add(r); counted.add(unparen((unparen((s as A.AssignStat).targets[0]) as A.IndexExpr).obj) as A.NameExpr); continue; }
        if (s.type === 'IfStat' && s.clauses.length === 1) {
          const g = guardRec(s.clauses[0].cond);
          const branches = [s.clauses[0].body, s.elseBody ?? []];
          if (g !== null && branches.every(b => b.every(x => asStore(x) !== null))) {
            const gs: Store[] = [];
            for (const b of branches) for (const x of b) { const st = { proto: p.id, stmt: x as A.AssignStat, rec: asStore(x)! }; gs.push(st); counted.add(unparen((unparen((x as A.AssignStat).targets[0]) as A.IndexExpr).obj) as A.NameExpr); seen.add(st.rec); }
            guards.push({ proto: p.id, stmt: s, rec: g, stores: gs }); seen.add(g);
            // the record name inside the condition
            const visitC = (n: any) => { if (!n || typeof n !== 'object') return; if (n.type === 'NameExpr') { counted.add(n); return; } for (const k of Object.keys(n)) if (k !== 'loc') visitC(n[k]); };
            visitC(s.clauses[0].cond);
            continue;
          }
        }
        // nested statement lists
        switch (s.type) {
          case 'DoStat': case 'WhileStat': case 'RepeatStat': case 'NumericForStat': case 'GenericForStat': visitStmts(s.body); break;
          case 'IfStat': for (const c of s.clauses) visitStmts(c.body); if (s.elseBody) visitStmts(s.elseBody); break;
        }
      }
    };
    // every statement list, nested functions included
    const lists: A.Stat[][] = [];
    const findFns = (n: any) => { if (!n || typeof n !== 'object') return; if (Array.isArray(n)) { n.forEach(findFns); return; } if (n.type === 'FunctionExpr') lists.push(n.body); for (const k of Object.keys(n)) if (k !== 'loc') { const x = n[k]; if (x && typeof x === 'object') findFns(x); } };
    lists.push(p.chunk.body); findFns(p.chunk.body);
    for (const l of lists) visitStmts(l);
    // any other reference observes the record
    for (const b of sc.bindings) {
      if (b.kind !== 'global') continue;
      const r = recordId(b.name); if (r === null) continue;
      for (const ref of b.refs) if (!counted.has(ref)) { observed.add(r); break; }
    }
  }
  // records written under a guard on an observed record are observed too (the guard decides them) — and a guard
  // that writes an observed record observes its own condition
  let grow = true;
  while (grow) {
    grow = false;
    for (const g of guards) {
      if (observed.has(g.rec)) continue;
      if (g.stores.some(s => observed.has(s.rec))) { observed.add(g.rec); grow = true; }
    }
  }
  const dead = new Set([...seen].filter(r => !observed.has(r)));
  if (!dead.size) return res;
  const drop = new Set<A.Stat>();
  for (const s of stores) if (dead.has(s.rec)) drop.add(s.stmt);
  for (const g of guards) if (dead.has(g.rec) && g.stores.every(s => dead.has(s.rec))) { drop.add(g.stmt); res.guards++; }
  for (const p of protos) {
    let n = 0;
    const filter = (list: A.Stat[]) => {
      for (let i = list.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
        const s = list[i];
        if (drop.has(s)) { list.splice(i, 1); n++; continue; }
        switch (s.type) {
          case 'DoStat': case 'WhileStat': case 'RepeatStat': case 'NumericForStat': case 'GenericForStat': filter(s.body); break;
          case 'IfStat': for (const c of s.clauses) filter(c.body); if (s.elseBody) filter(s.elseBody); break;
        }
      }
    };
    const findFns = (x: any) => { if (!x || typeof x !== 'object') return; if (Array.isArray(x)) { x.forEach(findFns); return; } if (x.type === 'FunctionExpr') filter(x.body); for (const k of Object.keys(x)) if (k !== 'loc') { const y = x[k]; if (y && typeof y === 'object') findFns(y); } };
    filter(p.chunk.body); findFns(p.chunk.body);
    if (n) res.changed.add(p.id);
  }
  res.stores = stores.filter(s => dead.has(s.rec)).length;
  res.records = dead.size;
  res.notes.push(`${res.stores} store(s) into ${dead.size} dump record(s) and ${res.guards} one-time patch guard(s) removed: the residual program never reads these records otherwise (self-modifying bytecode leftovers)` + (observed.size ? `; ${observed.size} record(s) still read at run time keep their stores` : ''));
  return res;
}

export type { OpcodeReport, DispatchTree, HandlerInfo, VmRoles, ConstantsReport, StringConst, NumberConst, ArrayConst, DecoderCandidate, PatternResult, PatternMatch, XrefBinding };

export interface CleanOptions {
  foldConstants?: boolean;
  recoverStrings?: boolean;
  removeDeadCode?: boolean;
  /** inline literal locals + pure aliases (local f = string.byte) */
  propagate?: boolean;
  /** drop never-read locals / assignments (junk) */
  removeUnusedLocals?: boolean;
  /** role-based renaming of obfuscated identifiers */
  rename?: RenameMode;
  /** drop redundant parentheses (printer re-adds the required ones) */
  stripParens?: boolean;
  /** while-break -> if, repeat-until-true -> do, opaque state-variable guards -> if/else */
  controlFlow?: boolean;
  rounds?: number;
  /** flow-sensitive constant/copy propagation (default on with propagate) */
  constFlow?: boolean;
  /** read-only global names (treated as constants by constFlow), e.g. specialiser record names */
  constGlobals?: (name: string) => boolean;
  /** fold hooks for read-only tables: `T[k]` / `#T` -> literal (VM specialiser) */
  constIndex?: (obj: A.Expr, key: A.Expr) => A.Expr | null;
  constLen?: (obj: A.Expr) => A.Expr | null;

  deadStores?: boolean;

  pureIndex?: boolean;
  /** promote register-file tables (`local R = table.create(n)` accessed by literal slots) to locals (VM residual code) */
  promoteRegisters?: boolean;
  /** state-machine unflattener limits / diagnostics */
  unflatten?: UnflattenOptions;

  packHelper?: (callee: A.Expr) => boolean;
  /** collects pass diagnostics (register promotion, multiple-results fusion) when given */
  diagnostics?: string[];
}

export interface CleanStats {
  folded: number; mbaFolded: number; charCalls: number; concatChains: number;
  prunedBranches: number; removedStmts: number;
  propagated: number; aliases: number; removedLocals: number; removedAssigns: number; renamed: number; parens: number;
  loopsToIf: number; guardsFolded: number; guardsMerged: number; blocksFlattened: number;

  guardConsts: number;
  /** flattened state-machine loops rebuilt as structured code */
  cffUnflattened: number;
  /** temporaries forwarded into their single use (copy propagation) */
  forwarded: number;
  /** reads replaced by flow-sensitive constant/copy propagation */
  constFlow: number;
  /** small literal-bound for-loops unrolled */
  unrolled: number;
  /** assignments to locals that are dead afterwards, removed */
  deadStores?: number;
  /** register-file slots promoted to locals */
  promoted?: number;
  /** multiple-results / varargs register ranges fused into calls, returns and constructors */
  multret?: number;
}

  code: string;
  rounds: number;
  stats: CleanStats;
  renameMap: Array<{ from: string; to: string; line: number; kind: string }>;
  parseErrors: number;

/** Parse + run the cleanup pipeline, return readable source. */
export function clean(src: string, opts: CleanOptions = {}): CleanResult {
  // explicit `undefined` (e.g. an omitted tool argument) must not override a default
  const given = Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(opts).filter(([, v]) => v !== undefined)) as CleanOptions;
  const o = { foldConstants: true, recoverStrings: true, removeDeadCode: true, propagate: true, removeUnusedLocals: true, rename: 'none' as RenameMode, stripParens: true, controlFlow: true, rounds: 8, ...given };
  const { chunk, errors } = parse(src);
  const stats: CleanStats = { folded: 0, mbaFolded: 0, charCalls: 0, concatChains: 0, prunedBranches: 0, removedStmts: 0, propagated: 0, aliases: 0, removedLocals: 0, removedAssigns: 0, renamed: 0, parens: 0, loopsToIf: 0, guardsFolded: 0, guardsMerged: 0, blocksFlattened: 0, guardConsts: 0, cffUnflattened: 0, forwarded: 0, constFlow: 0, unrolled: 0 };
  let rounds = 0;
  const round = (): number => {
    rounds++;
    let changed = 0;
    const aliases = analyzeAliases(chunk);
    if (o.recoverStrings) { const s = recoverStrings(chunk, { resolveStrAlias: aliases.resolveStr }); stats.charCalls += s.charCalls; stats.concatChains += s.concatChains; changed += s.charCalls + s.concatChains; }
    if (o.foldConstants) { const s = fold(chunk, { resolveBitAlias: aliases.resolveBit, resolveStrAlias: aliases.resolveStr, constIndex: o.constIndex, constLen: o.constLen }); stats.folded += s.folded; stats.mbaFolded += s.mbaFolded; changed += s.folded; }
    if (o.removeDeadCode) { const s = eliminateDeadCode(chunk); stats.prunedBranches += s.prunedBranches; stats.removedStmts += s.removedStmts; changed += s.prunedBranches + s.removedStmts; }
    if (o.controlFlow) {
      const l = loopOnce(chunk) + unrollSwitchFor(chunk) + unrollSwitchLoops(chunk); stats.loopsToIf += l; changed += l;
      const g = foldGuards(chunk); stats.guardsFolded += g.folded; stats.guardsMerged += g.merged; changed += g.folded + g.merged;
      const gc = guardConstProp(chunk); stats.guardConsts += gc; changed += gc;
      const u = unflattenStateLoops(chunk, o.unflatten); stats.cffUnflattened += u; changed += u + simplifyWhileTrue(chunk);
    }
    if (o.propagate) { const s = propagateConstants(chunk); stats.propagated += s.propagated; stats.aliases += s.aliases; changed += s.propagated + s.aliases; }
    if (o.propagate && o.constFlow !== false) { const c = constFlow(chunk, { constGlobals: o.constGlobals }); stats.constFlow += c; changed += c; }
    if (o.unrollFor) {
      // loops whose body indexes a constant table (or the register file being promoted) by the loop variable fold away
      const wide = (o.constIndex || o.promoteRegisters) ? (f: A.NumericForStat): boolean => {
        let hit = false;
        walk(f.body, (m: any) => {
          if (hit || m.type !== 'IndexExpr') return;
          const ix = m.index; if (!ix || ix.type !== 'NameExpr' || ix.name !== f.var) return;
          if (o.constIndex && o.constIndex(m.obj, { type: 'NumberLit', value: 1, raw: '1' } as A.Expr) !== null) hit = true;
        });
        if (!hit && o.promoteRegisters && f.body.length <= 4) walk(f.body, (m: any) => { if (m.type === 'IndexExpr' && m.obj.type === 'NameExpr' && m.index.type === 'NameExpr') hit = true; });
        return hit;
      } : undefined;
      const u = unrollSmallFor(chunk, o.unrollFor, 60, wide); stats.unrolled += u; changed += u;
    }
    if (o.propagate) { const x = expandCompound(chunk); const f = forwardSubst(chunk); stats.forwarded += f; changed += f + x; }
    if (o.controlFlow) { const f = flattenDo(chunk) + mergeDeclAssign(chunk); stats.blocksFlattened += f; changed += f; }
    if (o.deadStores !== false && o.removeUnusedLocals) { const d = removeDeadStores(chunk, { pureIndex: o.pureIndex }); stats.deadStores = (stats.deadStores ?? 0) + d; changed += d; }
    if (o.packHelper) { const m = fuseMultret(chunk, { isPack: o.packHelper }); const n = m.fused + m.fixed; if (n) { stats.multret = (stats.multret ?? 0) + n; changed += n; } if (o.diagnostics && m.skipped.size) o.diagnostics.push(`round ${rounds}: multret kept: ` + [...m.skipped].map(([k, v]) => `${k} ×${v}`).join(', ')); }

  for (let r = 0; r < o.rounds; r++) if (round() === 0) break;
  let renameMap: CleanResult['renameMap'] = [];
  if (o.rename !== 'none') {
    const r = smartRename(chunk, o.rename);
    stats.renamed = r.renamed; renameMap = r.map;
    // unique names make local->local alias propagation safe; run a couple more rounds
    for (let r2 = 0; r2 < 2; r2++) if (round() === 0) break;
  }
  if (o.stripParens) stats.parens = stripParens(chunk);
  return { code: print(chunk), rounds, stats, renameMap, parseErrors: errors.length };
}

export interface FullReport {
  ok: boolean;
  metrics: Metrics;
  families: FamilyGuess[];
  vm: VMReport;
  callGraph: {
    functionCount: number;
    edgeCount: number;
    topExternalCalls: Array<{ name: string; count: number }>;
    functions: CallGraph['functions'];
    edges: CallGraph['edges'];
  };
  strings: { total: number; samples: Array<{ value: string; line?: number }> };
  aliases: Array<{ name: string; target: string }>;
  parseErrors: Array<{ message: string; line: number }>;
}

/** Full static analysis report over the ORIGINAL (unmodified) AST. */
export function analyze(src: string): FullReport {
  const { chunk, errors } = parse(src);
  const metrics = computeMetrics(src, chunk);
  const families = fingerprint(src, metrics);
  const vm = detectVM(chunk);
  const cg = buildCallGraph(chunk);
  const aliases = analyzeAliases(chunk);
  const strs = collectStrings(chunk);
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  const samples: Array<{ value: string; line?: number }> = [];
  for (const s of strs) { if (!seen.has(s.value)) { seen.add(s.value); samples.push(s); if (samples.length >= 200) break; } }
  return {
    ok: errors.length === 0,
    metrics,
    families,
    vm,
    callGraph: {
      functionCount: cg.functions.length,
      edgeCount: cg.edges.length,
      topExternalCalls: cg.externalCalls.slice(0, 40),
      functions: cg.functions,
      edges: cg.edges,
    },
    strings: { total: strs.length, samples },
    aliases: [...aliases.builtins.entries()].map(([name, target]) => ({ name, target })),
    parseErrors: errors.map(e => ({ message: e.message, line: e.line })),
  };
}

/** Tokenize only — for the raw token inspector tool. */
export function tokenize(src: string) {
  const { tokens, errors } = lex(src);
  return {
    tokens: tokens.map(t => ({ type: T[t.type], value: t.value, line: t.line, col: t.col, start: t.start, end: t.end })),
    errors,
  };
}
export interface OpcodeMapResult { report: OpcodeReport; code: string; cleaned: boolean; }
/** Dispatch-tree / opcode extraction. By default runs on the cleaned code so that
 *  handler line numbers match the Deobfuscate output (`code` is returned). */
export function mapOpcodes(src: string, opts: { clean?: boolean | CleanOptions; minLeaves?: number; maxTrees?: number } = {}): OpcodeMapResult {
  let code = src;
  const doClean = opts.clean !== false;
  if (doClean) code = clean(src, typeof opts.clean === 'object' ? opts.clean : { rename: 'obfuscated' }).code;
  const { chunk } = parse(code);
  return { report: extractOpcodes(chunk, { minLeaves: opts.minLeaves, maxTrees: opts.maxTrees }), code, cleaned: doClean };
}

/** literal inventory + decoder candidates over the given source */
export function constants(src: string, opts: Parameters<typeof findConstants>[1] = {}): ConstantsReport {
  return findConstants(parse(src).chunk, opts);
}

export interface FunctionSource { id: string; name: string; line: number; endLine: number; params: string[]; code: string; }
/** source of one function by callgraph id (f12), name, or a line inside it (innermost wins) */
export function getFunction(src: string, query: string | number): FunctionSource | null {
  const { chunk } = parse(src);
  const cg = buildCallGraph(chunk);
  const lineOf = (pos: number) => { let l = 1; for (let i = 0; i < pos && i < src.length; i++) if (src.charCodeAt(i) === 10) l++; return l; };
  // statement starts so `local function f` / `function a.b()` headers are included
  const headers = new Map<number, number>();
  const visit = (n: any) => {
    if (!n || typeof n !== 'object') return;
    if (Array.isArray(n)) { n.forEach(visit); return; }
    if ((n.type === 'LocalFunctionStat' || n.type === 'FunctionStat') && n.func?.loc) headers.set(n.func.loc.start, n.loc?.start ?? n.func.loc.start);
    if (n.type === 'LocalStat' && n.init?.length === 1 && n.init[0].type === 'FunctionExpr' && n.init[0].loc) headers.set(n.init[0].loc.start, n.loc?.start ?? n.init[0].loc.start);
    for (const k of Object.keys(n)) if (k !== 'loc') visit(n[k]);
  };
  visit(chunk);
  const fns = cg.functions.filter(f => f.id !== 'main');
  let f = typeof query === 'number' || /^\d+$/.test(String(query)) ? undefined : fns.find(x => x.id === query) ?? fns.find(x => x.name === query) ?? fns.find(x => x.name.endsWith('.' + query) || x.name.endsWith(':' + query));
  if (!f) {
    const line = Number(query);
    if (!isFinite(line)) return null;
    let best: typeof fns[number] | undefined;
    for (const x of fns) { const s = lineOf(x.start), e = lineOf(x.end); if (s <= line && line <= e && (!best || x.end - x.start < best.end - best.start)) best = x; }
    f = best;
  }
  if (!f) return null;
  const start = headers.get(f.start) ?? f.start;
  // also cover `function` keyword before the parameter list
  const kw = src.lastIndexOf('function', f.start);
  const s0 = Math.min(start, kw >= 0 && f.start - kw < 64 ? kw : start);
  return { id: f.id, name: f.name, line: lineOf(s0), endLine: lineOf(f.end), params: f.params, code: src.slice(s0, f.end) };
}

export interface BytecodeDisasm { format: 'luau' | 'lua51'; text: string; summary: Record<string, unknown>; }
/** Auto-detect Luau / Lua 5.1 bytecode and disassemble it (static parse only). */
export function disassembleBytecode(bytes: Uint8Array, opts: LuauDisasmOptions & { encoding?: 'auto' | 'plain' | 'roblox'; format?: 'auto' | 'luau' | 'lua51' } = {}): BytecodeDisasm {
  const fmt = opts.format ?? 'auto';
  if (fmt === 'lua51' || (fmt === 'auto' && detectLuaBytecode(bytes))) {
    const ch = parseLua51Bytecode(bytes);
    return { format: 'lua51', text: disassembleLua51(ch, { style: opts.style === 'luau' ? 'luac' : 'rich', hex: opts.hex, lift: opts.lift, constants: opts.constants }), summary: { functions: ch.all.length, littleEndian: ch.littleEndian, sizeNumber: ch.sizeNumber, trailing: ch.trailing, instructions: ch.all.reduce((n, p) => n + p.code.length, 0) } };
  }
  const ch = parseLuauBytecode(bytes, { encoding: opts.encoding });
  const s = summarizeLuau(ch);
  return { format: 'luau', text: disassembleLuau(ch, opts), summary: s as unknown as Record<string, unknown> };
}

export interface EmbeddedBytecode { line: number; via: string; format: string; length: number; preview: string; }
/** Scan every string literal (raw, and base64/hex decoded) for embedded Lua/Luau bytecode. */
export function findEmbeddedBytecode(src: string, opts: { max?: number } = {}): EmbeddedBytecode[] {
  const out: EmbeddedBytecode[] = [];
  const { tokens } = lex(src);
  for (const t of tokens) {
    if (t.type !== T.String || out.length >= (opts.max ?? 50)) continue;
    const v = t.cooked ?? '';
    if (v.length < 12) continue;
    const cands: Array<[string, Uint8Array]> = [['raw', Blob.latin1(v)]];
    if (/^[A-Za-z0-9+/=\s]+$/.test(v) && v.length % 4 === 0) { try { cands.push(['base64', Blob.b64decode(v.replace(/\s+/g, ''))]); } catch { /* not base64 */ } }
    if (/^[0-9a-fA-F\s]+$/.test(v) && v.replace(/\s+/g, '').length % 2 === 0) { try { cands.push(['hex', Blob.hexdecode(v)]); } catch { /* not hex */ } }
    for (const [via, b] of cands) {
      const lua = detectLuaBytecode(b);
      const fmt = lua ? lua.lua + ' bytecode' : looksLikeLuauBytecode(b) ? `Luau bytecode v${b[0]}` : '';
      if (fmt) { out.push({ line: t.line, via, format: fmt, length: b.length, preview: Blob.hexencode(b.subarray(0, 24), ' ') }); break; }
    }
  }
  return out;
}

/** static map of how the script boots, runs and exits (payload → deserializer → wrapper → interpreter → exits → entry) */
export function anatomy(src: string, opts: { clean?: boolean | CleanOptions; maxChunks?: number } = {}): VmAnatomy & { code?: string } {
  const code = opts.clean ? clean(src, typeof opts.clean === 'object' ? opts.clean : { rename: 'obfuscated' }).code : undefined;
  const { chunk } = parse(code ?? src);
  return { ...vmAnatomy(chunk, { maxChunks: opts.maxChunks }), code };
}

/** constant-fold a single expression (number/bit/string junk) — e.g. "bit32.bxor(0x5A ^ 3, 7) + #'abc'" */
export function simplifyExpression(expr: string, opts: CleanOptions = {}): { result: string; changed: boolean } {
  const src = 'return ' + expr;
  const out = clean(src, { rename: 'none', removeUnusedLocals: false, ...opts }).code.trim();
  const result = out.replace(/^return\s+/, '').replace(/;$/, '');
  return { result, changed: result.replace(/\s+/g, '') !== expr.replace(/\s+/g, '') };
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ VM specialiser (devirtualiser)
export { astRewrite, globalsFromEnv, compileRules, specializeVM, findVmShape, selectHandler, LuaDump, collectPatches, resolvePatchedReads };

export interface VmSpecializeOptions extends SpecializeOptions {
  /** extra expression rewrite rules applied after cleaning (metavariables: __name) */
  rewrites?: RewriteRule[];
  /** skip cleaning (raw residual state machines) */
  raw?: boolean;
  rounds?: number;
  rename?: RenameMode;
  /** unflattener limits (defaults tuned for residual VM code) */
  unflatten?: UnflattenOptions;
  /** rounds of run-time patch discovery for self-modifying bytecode (default 6, 0 = off) */
  patchRounds?: number;
  /** promote the interpreter's register table to locals in the residual code (default on) */
  registers?: boolean;
  /** substitute constant tables handed between protos (argument / upvalue pools of literals and globals; default on) */
  constPools?: boolean;
}
export interface VmSpecializedProto { id: string; instrs: number; blocks: number; code: string; structured: boolean; notes: string[]; stats?: CleanStats; }
export interface VmSpecializeResult { ok: boolean; notes: string[]; protos: VmSpecializedProto[]; code: string; patches: PatchSpec[]; }
const patchKey = (p: PatchSpec) => p.table + '|' + (p.anyKey || p.key === undefined ? '*' : (typeof p.key === 'number' ? 'n:' + p.key : 's:' + p.key));
/** merge patch lists; reports whether anything new was added */
function mergePatches(base: PatchSpec[], extra: PatchSpec[]): { list: PatchSpec[]; changed: boolean } {
  const m = new Map<string, PatchSpec>();
  for (const p of base) m.set(patchKey(p), { ...p, values: p.values.slice() });
  let changed = false;
  for (const p of extra) {
    const k = patchKey(p); const e = m.get(k);
    if (!e) { m.set(k, { ...p, values: p.values.slice() }); changed = true; continue; }
    for (const v of p.values) if (!e.values.some(x => x === v)) { e.values.push(v); changed = true; }
    if (p.dynamic && !e.dynamic) { e.dynamic = true; changed = true; }
  }
  return { list: [...m.values()], changed };
}
/** Devirtualise: residual program of the VM interpreter for every dumped proto, cleaned + structured.
 *  Self-modifying bytecode: stores into dump records found in the cleaned residual code are fed back
 *  (patch discovery rounds) — patched instructions get one variant per written value, and reads of a
 *  patched slot that are dominated by its store are resolved statically. */
export function vmSpecialize(src: string, dumpJson: unknown, opts: VmSpecializeOptions = {}): VmSpecializeResult {
  const rules = opts.rewrites?.length ? compileRules(opts.rewrites) : [];
  let patches: PatchSpec[] = (opts.patches ?? []).slice();
  const maxRounds = opts.raw ? 0 : (opts.patchRounds ?? 6);
  const patchNotes: string[] = [];
  const canon = (l: PatchSpec[]) => l.map(p => patchKey(p) + '=' + [...p.values].map(v => JSON.stringify(v)).sort().join(',') + (p.dynamic ? '+dyn' : '')).sort().join(';');
  let checked: PatchSpec[] = [];
  for (let outer = 0; ; outer++) {
    // patch discovery on the residual blocks: the stores into dump records reachable under the current
    // patch set become the next patch set, until it reproduces itself (least fixpoint from the user's patches)
    let r: ReturnType<typeof specializeVM> | null = null;
    if (maxRounds > 0) {
      const seen = new Set<string>();
      for (let round = 0; round < maxRounds * 2; round++) {
        r = specializeVM(src, dumpJson, { ...opts, patches, discover: true });
        if (!r.ok) break;
        const next = mergePatches(mergePatches(opts.patches ?? [], checked).list, r.discovered ?? []).list;
        const cur = canon(patches), nx = canon(next);
        if (nx === cur) break;
        r = null;
        if (seen.has(nx)) { patchNotes.push(`patch rounds oscillate: union of the last two patch sets used`); patches = mergePatches(patches, next).list; break; }
        seen.add(cur);
        patchNotes.push(`patch round ${patchNotes.length + 1}: ${next.length} written slot(s) of dump records (${next.filter(p => p.dynamic).length} with computed values)`);
        patches = next;
      }
    }
    if (!r) r = specializeVM(src, dumpJson, { ...opts, patches });
    const out: VmSpecializeResult = { ok: r.ok, notes: r.notes.slice(), protos: [], code: '', patches };
    if (!r.ok || !r.shape) return out;
    const R = r;
    const makeTarget = r.shape.makeTarget;
    const pcVar = r.shape.pcVar;
    const recordId = (nm: string): string | null => { if (!R.constNames.has(nm)) return null; const m = /^(?:K|PROTO)_(.+)$/.exec(nm); return m ? m[1] : null; };
    // the interpreter's varargs-pack helper(s), recognised structurally in the source

    if (!opts.raw) { try { packHelpers = findPackHelpers(parse(src).chunk); } catch { /* none */ } }
    const packHelper = packHelpers.size ? (e: A.Expr) => packHelpers.has(printExpr(e)) : undefined;
    // stage 1: clean every residual proto (state machines unflattened)
    const stage: Array<{ p: typeof r.protos[number]; chunk: A.Chunk | null; stats?: CleanStats; why: Set<string>; unflatten: UnflattenOptions }> = [];
    for (const p of r.protos) {
      const why = new Set<string>();
      const unflatten: UnflattenOptions = { maxGrowth: 4, maxStates: 20000, ...opts.unflatten, onFail: (m) => { why.add(m); opts.unflatten?.onFail?.(m); } };
      if (opts.raw) { stage.push({ p, chunk: null, why, unflatten }); continue; }
      const c1 = clean(p.code, { rename: 'none', unrollFor: 8, rounds: opts.rounds ?? 16, constGlobals: r.hooks.constGlobals, constIndex: r.hooks.constIndex, constLen: r.hooks.constLen, unflatten });
      stage.push({ p, chunk: parse(c1.code).chunk, stats: c1.stats, why, unflatten });
    }

      for (const s of stage) if (s.chunk) found.push(...collectPatches(s.chunk, recordId));
      const have = new Map(patches.map(p => [patchKey(p), p]));
      const extra: PatchSpec[] = [];

        if (h && (h.anyKey || h.key === undefined)) continue;
        const lits = f.values.filter(v => !h || !h.values.some(x => x === v));
        if (!h || lits.length) extra.push({ ...f, values: lits, dynamic: !h && f.dynamic });
      }
      if (extra.length) { patchNotes.push(`patch check: ${extra.length} store(s) found in the cleaned code outside the patch set (${extra.slice(0, 8).map(e => `K_${e.table}[${e.anyKey ? '*' : JSON.stringify(e.key)}]`).join(', ')}) — another round`); checked = mergePatches(checked, extra).list; patches = mergePatches(patches, extra).list; continue; }
    }
    // static resolution of patched-slot reads (store dominates the read)
    if (!opts.raw && patches.length) {
      const createdProto = (c: A.CallExpr): string | null => {
        const a0 = c.args[0];
        if (makeTarget && printExpr(c.callee) === makeTarget && a0 && a0.type === 'NameExpr' && /^PROTO_/.test(a0.name)) return a0.name.slice(6);
        if (c.callee.type === 'IndexExpr' && c.callee.obj.type === 'NameExpr' && c.callee.obj.name === 'PROTOS' && c.callee.index.type === 'NumberLit') return String(c.callee.index.value);
        return null;

    let multretTotal = 0;

          const id = a0.name.slice(6);
          m.callee = { type: 'IndexExpr', obj: { type: 'NameExpr', name: 'PROTOS' }, index: /^\d+$/.test(id) ? { type: 'NumberLit', value: Number(id), raw: id } : { type: 'StringLit', value: id, raw: JSON.stringify(id) } };

        const dbg = (globalThis as any).__prismDebugStage; if (typeof dbg === 'function') dbg(p.id, 'c2-input', print(chunk));
        const c2 = clean(print(chunk), { rename: opts.rename ?? 'none', unrollFor: 8, rounds: opts.registers === false ? 6 : 10, constGlobals: r.hooks.constGlobals, constIndex: r.hooks.constIndex, constLen: r.hooks.constLen, unflatten: s.unflatten, promoteRegisters: opts.registers !== false, pureIndex: true, packHelper: opts.registers !== false ? packHelper : undefined });

      codes.push({ s, code, cleaned: !!s.chunk });
    }
    // whole-program passes over the cleaned protos: constant pools handed from proto to proto (argument / upvalue

    if (!opts.raw && codes.some(c => c.cleaned)) {

'none', unrollFor: 8, rounds: 6, constGlobals: r.hooks.constGlobals, constIndex: r.hooks.constIndex, constLen: r.hooks.constLen, unflatten: x.c.s.unflatten, promoteRegisters: false, pureIndex: true, packHelper: opts.registers !== false ? packHelper : undefined });

    }
    if (multretTotal) patchNotes.push(`${multretTotal} multiple-results / varargs register range(s) fused back into calls, returns, assignments and table constructors (registers above an instruction's operands are taken as dead after it, as in compiled code)`);
    for (const { s, code, cleaned } of codes) {
      const p = s.p;

      const structured = cleaned && !new RegExp('\\b' + pcVar + '\\s*(<|==|~=|>)').test(code);

      out.protos.push({ id: p.id, instrs: p.instrs, blocks: p.blocks, code, structured, notes, stats: s.stats });
    }
    out.notes.push(...patchNotes);
    const patchLines = patches.length ? ['-- run-time written slots of dump records (self-modifying bytecode): ' + patches.length, ...patches.slice(0, 400).map(ps => `--   K_${ps.table}[${ps.anyKey || ps.key === undefined ? '*' : JSON.stringify(ps.key)}] <- ${ps.values.map(v => JSON.stringify(v)).join(' | ')}${ps.dynamic ? ' | <computed>' : ''}`)] : [];
    out.code = ['-- PRISM vm_specialize: residual program of the VM interpreter (one maker per proto).',
      '-- PROTOS[n](upvalues) returns the closure for proto n; PROTO_n / K_n are records of the dump.',
      ...out.notes.map(n => '-- ' + n), ...patchLines, 'local PROTOS = {}', ...out.protos.map(p => `-- proto ${p.id}: ${p.instrs} instructions, ${p.blocks} blocks${p.structured ? ', structured' : ', state machine kept'}\n` + p.code)].join('\n');
    return out;
  }
}

// PRISM deobfuscation runner for TEST-PRISM3
import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'fs';

// Adjust module resolution to find PRISM packages
const PRISM = '/data/prism/packages/core/src/index.ts';

// Dynamic import hack for tsx
const { analyze, clean, mapOpcodes, vmSpecialize, anatomy, findConstants, constants,
  findEmbeddedBytecode, detectVM, specializeVM, findVmShape, LuaDump, collectPatches }
  = await import(PRISM);

console.log('Metrics:', JSON.stringify(report.metrics, null, 2));
console.log('Families:', JSON.stringify(report.families, null, 2));
console.log('VM detection:', JSON.stringify(report.vm, null, 2));
console.log('Parse errors:', report.parseErrors.length);
console.log('Functions:', report.callGraph.functionCount);
console.log('Top external calls:', JSON.stringify(report.callGraph.topExternalCalls.slice(0, 20)));
console.log('Strings sample (first 20):', JSON.stringify(report.strings.samples.slice(0, 20)));

console.log('[+] Full report -> /data/analysis_report.json');

// Step 2: opcode map
console.log('\n=== OPCODE MAP ===');
try {
  const opcMap = mapOpcodes(src, { clean: true });
  console.log('Opcode report summary:');
  if (opcMap.report.trees) {
    for (const t of opcMap.report.trees.slice(0, 3)) {
      console.log(`  Tree at line ${t.line}: ${t.leaves} handlers, dispatch on: ${JSON.stringify(t.dispatch ?? 'unknown')}`);
    }
  }
  writeFileSync('/data/opcode_report.json', JSON.stringify(opcMap.report, null, 2));
  console.log('[+] Opcode report -> /data/opcode_report.json');
} catch(e) { console.error('mapOpcodes failed:', (e as Error).message); }

// Step 3: anatomy
console.log('\n=== ANATOMY ===');
try {
  const anat = anatomy(src, { clean: true });
  console.log('Anatomy:', JSON.stringify(anat, null, 2));
  writeFileSync('/data/anatomy.json', JSON.stringify(anat, null, 2));
} catch(e) { console.error('anatomy failed:', (e as Error).message); }

// Step 4: constants
console.log('\n=== CONSTANTS ===');

  console.log('Total numbers:', consts.numbers?.length);
  console.log('Sample strings:', JSON.stringify((consts.strings ?? []).slice(0, 30)));
  console.log('Sample numbers:', JSON.stringify((consts.numbers ?? []).slice(0, 20)));
  console.log('Decoders:', JSON.stringify(consts.decoders ?? []));
  writeFileSync('/data/constants.json', JSON.stringify(consts, null, 2));
  console.log('[+] Constants -> /data/constants.json');
} catch(e) { console.error('constants failed:', (e as Error).message); }

// Step 5: find dump JSON  
console.log('\n=== FINDING DUMP ===');

try {
  const found = LuaDumpInst.find(src);
  console.log('LuaDump.find result:', JSON.stringify(found));
} catch(e) { console.error('LuaDump.find failed:', (e as Error).message); }

// Step 2: vmSpecialize deobfuscation
import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'fs';

const { LuaDump, vmSpecialize, clean, specializeVM, findVmShape, selectHandler, analyze } =
  await import('/data/prism/packages/core/src/index.ts');

const src = readFileSync('/data/target.lua', 'utf8');
console.log(`[+] Source: ${src.length} chars`);

// Try to find dump
const dump = new LuaDump();
console.log('\n=== FINDING DUMP ===');
let dumpJson: unknown = null;
try {
  const found = dump.find(src);
  console.log('dump.find:', JSON.stringify(found));
} catch(e) { console.error('dump.find error:', (e as any).message?.slice(0,200)); }

try {
  const extracted = dump.extract(src);
  console.log('dump.extract keys:', extracted ? Object.keys(extracted) : 'null');
  if (extracted) {
    dumpJson = extracted;
    writeFileSync('/data/dump.json', JSON.stringify(extracted, null, 2));
    console.log('[+] Dump JSON -> /data/dump.json');
  }
} catch(e) { console.error('dump.extract error:', (e as any).message?.slice(0,200)); }

// Try findVmShape directly
console.log('\n=== FIND VM SHAPE ===');
try {
  const { chunk } = await import('/data/prism/packages/core/src/index.ts').then(m => (m as any).parse ? { chunk: (m as any).parse(src).chunk } : { chunk: null });
  if (chunk) {
    const shape = findVmShape(chunk);
    console.log('VM shape:', JSON.stringify(shape, (k, v) => typeof v === 'function' ? '[fn]' : v, 2));
    writeFileSync('/data/vmshape.json', JSON.stringify(shape, (k, v) => typeof v === 'function' ? '[fn]' : v, 2));
  }
} catch(e) { console.error('findVmShape error:', (e as any).message?.slice(0,200)); }

// Try vmSpecialize without dump first
console.log('\n=== VM SPECIALIZE (auto-dump) ===');
try {
  const result = vmSpecialize(src, dumpJson, {
    patchRounds: 6,
    registers: true,
    constPools: true,
    rename: 'obfuscated',
    rounds: 16,
  });
  console.log('ok:', result.ok);
  console.log('notes:', result.notes.slice(0, 20));
  console.log('protos count:', result.protos.length);
  if (result.protos.length > 0) {
    console.log('First proto id:', result.protos[0].id);
    console.log('First proto structured:', result.protos[0].structured);
    console.log('First proto notes:', result.protos[0].notes);
    console.log('First proto code (first 2000 chars):');
    console.log(result.protos[0].code.slice(0, 2000));
    // Write full output
    writeFileSync('/data/deobf_full.lua', result.code);
    console.log('\n[+] Full deobfuscated -> /data/deobf_full.lua (' + result.code.length + ' chars)');
    // Also write per-proto
    for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(result.protos.length, 5); i++) {
      const p = result.protos[i];
      writeFileSync(`/data/proto_${p.id}.lua`, p.code);
      console.log(`[+] Proto ${p.id}: ${p.instrs} instrs, ${p.blocks} blocks, structured=${p.structured}, ${p.code.length} chars`);
    }
  }
} catch(e) {
  const err = e as Error;
  console.error('vmSpecialize error:', err.message?.slice(0, 500));
  console.error(err.stack?.slice(0, 1000));
}

console.log('\n[done]');

// Reader for runtime/table dumps (JSON) — the format written by PRISM's Python-port dump hooks:
//   table   {"$id": n, "$arr": [v1, v2, …], "$map": {"key": v, …}, "$meta": t}
//   ref     {"$ref": n}          function {"$fn": "string.byte"}
//   bytes   {"$bytes": "hex"}    buffer   {"$buffer": "hex"}
// Plain JSON (lists = 1-based Lua arrays, objects = maps) is accepted as well.
import type * as A from '../ast.js';

export type DumpVal = unknown;
type Obj = Record<string, any>;
const isObj = (v: unknown): v is Obj => !!v && typeof v === 'object' && !Array.isArray(v);
const hexLatin1 = (h: string) => { let s = ''; for (let i = 0; i + 1 < h.length; i += 2) s += String.fromCharCode(parseInt(h.slice(i, i + 2), 16)); return s; };
const utf8Latin1 = (s: string) => { if (/^[\x00-\x7f]*$/.test(s)) return s; return Array.from(new TextEncoder().encode(s), b => String.fromCharCode(b)).join(''); };
const NUMKEY = /^-?(\d+(\.\d+)?|\.\d+)(e[+-]?\d+)?$/i;

export type Scalar =
  | { kind: 'nil' } | { kind: 'bool'; value: boolean } | { kind: 'num'; value: number } | { kind: 'str'; value: string }
  | { kind: 'fn'; name: string } | { kind: 'buffer'; hex: string } | { kind: 'table'; id: string };

export class LuaDump {
  readonly ids = new Map<number, Obj>();
  private synth = new WeakMap<object, string>();
  private nextSynth = 1;
  constructor(readonly root: unknown) { this.index(root, 0); }
  private index(x: unknown, depth: number) {
    if (depth > 4000) return;
    if (Array.isArray(x)) { for (const v of x) this.index(v, depth + 1); return; }
    if (!isObj(x)) return;
    if (typeof x.$id === 'number') this.ids.set(x.$id, x);
    for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(x)) {
      if (k === '$ref' || k === '$fn' || k === '$bytes' || k === '$buffer' || k === '$id') continue;
      this.index(v, depth + 1);
    }
  }
  deref(v: unknown): unknown { return isObj(v) && typeof v.$ref === 'number' ? this.ids.get(v.$ref) : v; }
  isTable(v: unknown): boolean {
    const d = this.deref(v);
    if (Array.isArray(d)) return true;
    return isObj(d) && d.$fn === undefined && d.$bytes === undefined && d.$buffer === undefined;
  }
  /** stable identity of a table value */
  tableId(v: unknown): string {
    const d = this.deref(v) as any;
    if (isObj(d) && typeof d.$id === 'number') return String(d.$id);
    let s = this.synth.get(d); if (!s) { s = 's' + this.nextSynth++; this.synth.set(d, s); } return s;
  }
  scalar(v: unknown): Scalar {
    const d = this.deref(v);
    if (d === null || d === undefined) return { kind: 'nil' };
    if (typeof d === 'boolean') return { kind: 'bool', value: d };
    if (typeof d === 'number') return { kind: 'num', value: d };
    if (typeof d === 'string') return { kind: 'str', value: utf8Latin1(d) };
    if (isObj(d)) {
      if (typeof d.$bytes === 'string') return { kind: 'str', value: hexLatin1(d.$bytes) };
      if (typeof d.$fn === 'string') return { kind: 'fn', name: d.$fn };
      if (typeof d.$buffer === 'string') return { kind: 'buffer', hex: d.$buffer };
    }
    return { kind: 'table', id: this.tableId(d) };
  }
  /** Lua t[key] */
  get(t: unknown, key: number | string | boolean): unknown {

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Decode the Luraph-style bytecode from target.lua"""
import re, json, struct, sys

with open('/data/target.lua', 'r', encoding='latin1') as f:
    src = f.read()

print(f'[+] Source length: {len(src)} chars')

# Find ALL long bracket strings
for m in re.finditer(r'\[=*(\[)(.*?)(\])(=*)\]', src, re.DOTALL):
    lb = m.group(2)
    print(f'[+] Long bracket at {m.start()}: {len(lb)} chars')

# Extract the main long bracket
lb_start = src.index('[[')
lb_end = src.index(']]', lb_start+2)
lb_data = src[lb_start+2:lb_end]
print(f'[+] Main data: {len(lb_data)} chars')
bytes_data = lb_data.encode('latin1')
print(f'[+] Byte range: {min(bytes_data)} - {max(bytes_data)}')

# Try different decoding schemes
# Scheme 1: Luraph base encoding (byte - 33 gives 0-93 range values)
# This encodes each byte of the binary data as char+33
# But some bytes need escaping

def try_decode_luraph(data: bytes) -> bytes | None:
    """Try Luraph-style: escape byte 0x01, rest shifted by some offset"""
    # Find the most likely escape byte by frequency analysis
    freqs = [0] * 256
    for b in data:
        freqs[b] += 1
    
    print(f'\n[Decode] Byte frequencies (top 10):')
    top = sorted(enumerate(freqs), key=lambda x: -x[1])[:10]
    for b, cnt in top:
        print(f'  0x{b:02x} ({chr(b) if 32<=b<127 else "?"!r}): {cnt}')
    
    # Try escape byte = 0x21 (!) with decode: if byte==0x21, next_byte - 1
    # Otherwise, the byte itself is the value
    out = bytearray()
    i = 0
    ESC = 0x21  # '!'
    while i < len(data):
        b = data[i]
        if b == ESC:
            if i+1 < len(data):
                out.append(data[i+1] - 1)
                i += 2
            else:
                break
        else:
            out.append(b)
            i += 1
    return bytes(out)

decoded = try_decode_luraph(bytes_data)
print(f'\n[+] Decoded (escape=0x21) length: {len(decoded)}')
print(f'[+] First 100 decoded bytes: {list(decoded[:100])}')

# Check if decoded data has Lua table structure
# In Luraph, the bytecode is typically stored as Lua tables
# Check for patterns that indicate proto arrays
def find_proto_boundaries(data: bytes) -> list:
    """Try to find proto boundaries in decoded data"""
    # In many Luraph VMs, each proto starts with a count (number of instructions)
    # followed by instruction data
    results = []
    # Look for reasonably-sized instruction counts (e.g., 1-10000)
    for i in range(0, min(len(data)-4, 100)):
        # Try reading as little-endian uint32
        val = struct.unpack_from('<I', data, i)[0]
        if 1 <= val <= 10000:
            results.append((i, val))
    return results[:20]

boundaries = find_proto_boundaries(decoded)
print(f'\nPossible proto count values at start: {boundaries[:10]}')

# Save decoded data for further analysis
with open('/data/decoded_bytecode.bin', 'wb') as f:
    f.write(decoded)
print(f'[+] Raw decoded -> /data/decoded_bytecode.bin')

# Also try: subtract 33 from each byte (simple shift)
decoded2 = bytes([b - 33 for b in bytes_data if b >= 33])
print(f'\n[Shift-33 decode] First 50 values: {list(decoded2[:50])}')

# Try: Lua chunk format detection
# Standard Lua 5.1 bytecode starts with \x1bLua
# Luau starts with specific header
for name, dec in [('escape-21', decoded), ('shift-33', decoded2)]:
    if dec[:4] == b'\x1bLua':
        print(f'[!] {name}: Looks like Lua 5.1 bytecode!')
    elif dec[0:1] == b'\x06':
        print(f'[!] {name}: Might be Luau bytecode (starts with 0x06)!')
    else:
        print(f'[?] {name}: First bytes: {list(dec[:8])}')

print('\n[+] Done decoding analysis')

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import re, json, struct, sys

with open('/data/target.lua', 'r', encoding='latin1') as f:
    src = f.read()

# Extract ALL long brackets
print(f'[+] Source: {len(src)} chars')
lb_all = []
for m in re.finditer(r'\[=*(\[)(.*?)(\]=*\])', src, re.DOTALL):
    full = m.group(0)
    # Only match [[...]] (no = signs)
    if full.startswith('[[') and full.endswith(']]'):
        content = full[2:-2]
        lb_all.append((m.start(), content))
        print(f'  Long bracket at {m.start()}: {len(content)} chars')

# Sort by size, decode each
def decode_lb(data_str: str, label: str) -> dict:
    raw = data_str.encode('latin1')
    # Method 1: shift-33 (subtract 33 from each byte)
    shifted = bytes([b - 33 for b in raw])
    # Method 2: escape-based (! = escape, next byte - 1)
    unescaped = bytearray()
    i = 0
    while i < len(raw):
        if raw[i] == 0x21 and i+1 < len(raw):
            unescaped.append(raw[i+1] - 1)
            i += 2
        else:
            unescaped.append(raw[i])
            i += 1
    
    result = {'label': label, 'raw_len': len(raw), 'shifted': shifted, 'unescaped': bytes(unescaped)}
    return result

for pos, content in lb_all:
    r = decode_lb(content, f'lb_{pos}')
    label = r['label']
    for method, data in [('shifted', r['shifted']), ('unescaped', r['unescaped'])]:
        outfile = f'/data/{label}_{method}.bin'
        with open(outfile, 'wb') as f:
            f.write(data)
        # Check for Lua magic bytes
        lua_magic = data[:4] == b'\x1bLua'
        luau_magic = len(data) > 0 and data[0] == 0x06
        note = ''
        if lua_magic: note = ' *** LUA 5.1 BYTECODE ***'
        elif luau_magic: note = ' ** LUAU BYTECODE **'
        print(f'  {label} {method}: {len(data)} bytes{note} -> {outfile}')
        if lua_magic or luau_magic:
            print(f'    First 32 bytes: {list(data[:32])}')

print()
# Try to decode as Luraph number stream (variable length encoding)
# Luraph uses: if first byte has high bit set, it's a 1-byte value (val & 0x7f)
# otherwise 4-byte LE uint32
def decode_luraph_numbers(data: bytes) -> list:
    nums = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(data):
        b = data[i]
        if b & 0x80:
            nums.append(b & 0x7f)
            i += 1
        else:
            if i + 4 <= len(data):
                val = struct.unpack_from('<I', data, i)[0]
                nums.append(val)
                i += 4
            else:
                break
    return nums

# Try the largest long bracket with both methods
largest = max(lb_all, key=lambda x: len(x[1]))
pos, content = largest
print(f'[+] Analyzing largest LB at {pos} ({len(content)} chars)...')
raw = content.encode('latin1')
shifted = bytes([b - 33 for b in raw])
nums = decode_luraph_numbers(shifted)
print(f'  Luraph number stream: {len(nums)} values')
print(f'  First 30: {nums[:30]}')
# Try reading as proto sequence
# First number is likely proto count or main proto instruction count
if nums:
    print(f'  First value (proto count?): {nums[0]}')
    # If nums[0] is a reasonable proto count (1-500), try parsing protos
    if 1 <= nums[0] <= 500:
        print(f'  Attempting proto parse with {nums[0]} protos...')
        try:
            protos = []
            idx = 1
            for pn in range(int(nums[0])):
                # Each proto: num_params, num_upvals, num_instrs, [instrs...], ...
                if idx >= len(nums): break
                n_instrs = nums[idx]; idx += 1
                instrs = nums[idx:idx+n_instrs]; idx += n_instrs
                protos.append({'instrs': instrs[:20], 'n': n_instrs})
                if pn < 3:
                    print(f'    Proto {pn}: {n_instrs} instrs, first 5: {instrs[:5]}')
            print(f'  Parsed {len(protos)} protos')
        except Exception as e:
            print(f'  Parse failed: {e}')

print('\n[+] Done')

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Decode the 91,659-byte base85 payload from target.lua"""
import re, json, struct, sys, os

with open('/data/target.lua', 'r', encoding='latin1') as f:
    src = f.read()
with open('/data/cleaned.lua', 'r', encoding='latin1') as f:
    cleaned = f.read()

# Find the payload string in the cleaned source (at pos 31894)
# It's a 91,659-byte string literal
# Look for the opening quote near pos 31893
pos = 31890
while pos < 32000 and cleaned[pos] != '"':
    pos += 1
print(f'String starts at pos {pos} in cleaned')

# Extract the Lua string (handle escape sequences)
# Find the closing quote (tricky because of escaped quotes)
string_start = pos + 1
i = string_start
payload_chars = []
while i < len(cleaned):
    c = cleaned[i]
    if c == '\\' and i+1 < len(cleaned):
        nc = cleaned[i+1]
        if nc == '\\': payload_chars.append('\\'); i += 2
        elif nc == '"': payload_chars.append('"'); i += 2
        elif nc == "'": payload_chars.append("'"); i += 2
        elif nc == 'n': payload_chars.append('\n'); i += 2
        elif nc == 'r': payload_chars.append('\r'); i += 2
        elif nc == 't': payload_chars.append('\t'); i += 2
        elif nc.isdigit():
            # \ddd decimal escape
            j = i+1
            while j < i+4 and j < len(cleaned) and cleaned[j].isdigit(): j += 1
            payload_chars.append(chr(int(cleaned[i+1:j])))
            i = j
        else: payload_chars.append(nc); i += 2
    elif c == '"':
        break  # end of string
    else:
        payload_chars.append(c); i += 1

payload_str = ''.join(payload_chars)
payload_bytes = payload_str.encode('latin1')
print(f'Payload: {len(payload_str)} chars, {len(payload_bytes)} bytes')
print(f'First 50 chars: {repr(payload_str[:50])}')
print(f'Byte range: {min(payload_bytes)}-{max(payload_bytes)}')

# Try base85 decode
def base85_decode(data: bytes) -> bytes | None:
    """Standard ASCII85/base85: each 5 chars = 4 bytes, chars in [33..117]"""
    out = bytearray()
    # Remove whitespace and handle 'z' shorthand (all zeros)
    i = 0
    while i < len(data):
        # Collect 5 chars
        group = []
        while i < len(data) and len(group) < 5:
            b = data[i]
            if b < 33 or b > 117:
                return None  # invalid char for base85
            group.append(b - 33)
            i += 1
        if len(group) < 5:
            # Pad last group
            if not group: break
            pad = 5 - len(group)
            for _ in range(pad): group.append(84)  # 'u'-33=84
            val = 0
            for d in group:
                val = val * 85 + d
            # Only take (5-pad)*1 bytes
            for j in range(4 - pad + 1, 5):
                b = (val >> (8*(4-j))) & 0xFF
                out.append(b)
        else:
            val = 0
            for d in group:
                val = val * 85 + d
            if val > 0xFFFFFFFF: return None  # overflow
            out.append((val >> 24) & 0xFF)
            out.append((val >> 16) & 0xFF)
            out.append((val >> 8) & 0xFF)
            out.append(val & 0xFF)
    return bytes(out)

# Check if chars are in base85 range
valid_b85 = all(33 <= b <= 117 for b in payload_bytes)
print(f'\nAll chars in base85 range [33,117]: {valid_b85}')
print(f'Chars outside range: {[(i,b,chr(b)) for i,b in enumerate(payload_bytes[:200]) if not (33<=b<=117)][:10]}')

if valid_b85:
    decoded = base85_decode(payload_bytes)
    if decoded:
        print(f'Base85 decoded: {len(decoded)} bytes')
        print(f'First 32 bytes: {list(decoded[:32])}')
        with open('/data/payload_b85.bin', 'wb') as f:
            f.write(decoded)
        print(f'Saved -> /data/payload_b85.bin')
else:
    # Find max char value
    max_b = max(payload_bytes)
    print(f'Max byte: {max_b} = {chr(max_b)!r}')
    # Try extended base (0 to max-33)
    base = max_b - 33 + 1
    print(f'Trying base-{base} (chars 33..{max_b})')

# Try shift-33 and interpret as 4-byte LE uint32 stream
shifted = bytes([b - 33 for b in payload_bytes])
print(f'\nShift-33 first 100 values: {list(shifted[:100])}')

# Parse as 4-byte LE integers
if len(shifted) % 4 == 0:
    ints = [struct.unpack_from('<I', shifted, i)[0] for i in range(0, len(shifted), 4)]
    print(f'As 4-byte LE ints ({len(ints)} values), first 20: {ints[:20]}')

# Also try: each pair of chars = 1 value (Luraph base-91)
def decode_base91(data: bytes) -> list:
    """Base-91 uses chars 33-123, each pair decodes to a 13-bit value"""
    vals = []
    i = 0
    while i+1 < len(data):
        v = (data[i] - 33) + (data[i+1] - 33) * 91
        vals.append(v)
        i += 2
    return vals

base91_vals = decode_base91(payload_bytes)
print(f'\nBase-91 pairs ({len(base91_vals)} values), first 30: {base91_vals[:30]}')

print('\n[done]')

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Decode Luraph payload - every 5th char is separator 'd'"""
import re, json, struct

with open('/data/cleaned.lua','r',encoding='latin1') as f:
    cleaned = f.read()

# Extract payload string (at pos 31894)
pos = 31894
while cleaned[pos] != '"': pos += 1
s = pos + 1; e = s
while True:
    if cleaned[e] == '\\': e += 2
    elif cleaned[e] == '"': break
    else: e += 1
payload = cleaned[s:e].encode('latin1')
# Unescape
import codecs
try:
    payload = bytes([ord(c) for c in cleaned[s:e].replace('\\\\','\x00').replace('\\"','"').replace('\x00','\\')])
except:
    pass

# Just use raw bytes from cleaned source directly
payload_raw = []
i = s
while i < e:
    c = cleaned[i]
    if c == '\\':
        nc = cleaned[i+1]
        if nc == '\\': payload_raw.append(92); i += 2
        elif nc == '"': payload_raw.append(34); i += 2
        elif nc == "'": payload_raw.append(39); i += 2
        elif nc.isdigit():
            j = i+1
            while j < i+4 and cleaned[j].isdigit(): j += 1
            payload_raw.append(int(cleaned[i+1:j])); i = j
        else: payload_raw.append(ord(nc)); i += 2
    else:
        payload_raw.append(ord(c)); i += 1

payload_bytes = bytes(payload_raw)
print(f'Payload: {len(payload_bytes)} bytes, range {min(payload_bytes)}-{max(payload_bytes)}')

# Verify 5th-char separator pattern
shifted = [b - 33 for b in payload_bytes]
sep_vals = [shifted[i] for i in range(4, len(shifted), 5)]
uniq_seps = set(sep_vals)
print(f'Separator values (every 5th): unique={uniq_seps}, count={len(sep_vals)}')

# If all 67, confirmed base90 with separator
if uniq_seps == {67}:
    print('CONFIRMED: separator is always 67 (d=100). Extracting data quads...')
    quads = []
    for i in range(0, len(shifted)-4, 5):
        quads.append([shifted[i], shifted[i+1], shifted[i+2], shifted[i+3]])
    print(f'Total quads: {len(quads)}')
    print(f'First 10 quads: {quads[:10]}')
    
    # Try: each quad = LE 32-bit number using base 90
    # v[0] + v[1]*90 + v[2]*90^2 + v[3]*90^3
    def quad_to_int_le(q):
        return q[0] + q[1]*90 + q[2]*8100 + q[3]*729000
    
    nums_le = [quad_to_int_le(q) for q in quads]
    print(f'LE base-90 ints, first 20: {nums_le[:20]}')
    
    # Try: big-endian
    def quad_to_int_be(q):
        return q[3] + q[2]*90 + q[1]*8100 + q[0]*729000
    nums_be = [quad_to_int_be(q) for q in quads]
    print(f'BE base-90 ints, first 20: {nums_be[:20]}')
    
    # What if first value is number of protos or instructions?
    print(f'\nFirst LE value: {nums_le[0]} (possible proto count?)')
    print(f'First BE value: {nums_be[0]}')
    
    # If nums_le[0] is a reasonable proto count
    n0 = nums_le[0]
    if 1 <= n0 <= 300:
        print(f'\nAttempting proto parse with {n0} protos...')
        idx = 1
        protos = []
        ok = True
        for pn in range(n0):
            if idx >= len(nums_le): ok = False; break
            n_instrs = nums_le[idx]; idx += 1
            if n_instrs > 50000 or n_instrs < 0: ok = False; break
            instrs = nums_le[idx:idx+n_instrs]; idx += n_instrs
            protos.append({'n_instrs': n_instrs, 'instrs': instrs[:5]})
            if pn < 5:

        if ok:

    # Also try first value as instruction count directly

            instrs = nums_be[1:1+be_val]

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Analyze the interpreter section to map opcodes to semantics"""
import re, json

with open('/data/cleaned.lua','r',encoding='latin1') as f:
    lines = f.readlines()

# Interpreter: L1408-2918 (0-indexed: 1407-2917)
interp = lines[1407:2918]
print(f'Interpreter: {len(interp)} lines')

# Find all "if elem8 == N then" or "elseif elem8 == N then" patterns
opcode_pattern = re.compile(r'(?:if|elseif)\s+(?:not\s+)?elem8\s*([><=!]{1,3})\s*(\d+)\s+then')

opcode_actions = {}  # opcode -> code lines
current_ops = []
current_lines = []

for li, line in enumerate(interp):
    m = opcode_pattern.search(line)
    if m:
        op_cond = m.group(1)
        op_val = int(m.group(2))
        # Extract simple equality checks only
        if op_cond == '==' and 'not' not in line.split('then')[0]:
            current_ops.append(op_val)
            current_lines.append(li + 1408)

print(f'\nFound {len(current_ops)} opcode dispatch points')
print('Opcode values:', sorted(set(current_ops)))

# For each opcode, extract the code block following it
# Simple approach: look at next 5 lines after each dispatch
opcode_blocks = {}
for idx, (op, start_li) in enumerate(zip(current_ops, current_lines)):
    # Get next 8 lines
    rel_start = start_li - 1408  # relative line in interp
    block = []
    depth = 0
    for rel_li in range(rel_start + 1, min(rel_start + 15, len(interp))):
        bl = interp[rel_li].strip()
        if not bl: continue
        block.append(bl)
        # Stop at next elseif/else/end that's at same depth
        if bl.startswith('elseif ') or bl == 'else' or bl == 'end':
            break
        if len(block) >= 8: break
    opcode_blocks[op] = block

# Print semantics for each opcode
print('\n=== OPCODE SEMANTICS ===')
for op in sorted(opcode_blocks.keys()):
    code = ' | '.join(opcode_blocks[op][:3])
    print(f'  OP {op:3d}: {code}')

# Save full opcode map
with open('/data/opcode_map.json','w') as f:
    json.dump({'opcodes': opcode_blocks}, f, indent=2)
print(f'\nSaved opcode_map.json')

# Also look for key variable names to understand the VM model
print('\n=== KEY VARIABLE PATTERNS ===')
patterns = {
    'ret5[': 'Register write',
    '= ret5[': 'Register read',
    'elem6[num9]': 'dest register',
    'elem3[num9]': 'src/const index',
    'elem7[num9]': 'immediate/jump',
    'j[num9]': 'second src',
    'e9': 'extra field',
    'var61': 'table var',
    'var62': 'numeric var',
    'var63': 'function return',
    'k[': 'constant table',
    'num9': 'PC counter',
    'elem8': 'opcode',
}
for line in interp:
    for pat, desc in patterns.items():
        if pat in line:
            break

# Count variable appearances
from collections import Counter
all_text = ''.join(interp)
var_counts = Counter()
for var in ['ret5', 'elem6', 'elem3', 'elem7', 'num9', 'var61', 'var62', 'var63', 'var53', 'k[', 'elem8']:
    cnt = all_text.count(var)
    var_counts[var] = cnt

print('Variable usage in interpreter:')
for var, cnt in var_counts.most_common():
    print(f'  {var}: {cnt}')

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Decode long brackets in original source as ASCII85 / other encodings"""
import re, json, struct

with open('/data/target.lua','r',encoding='latin1') as f:
    src = f.read()

# Find ALL long bracket strings
lb_pattern = re.compile(r'\[=*(\[)(.*?)\]=*\]', re.DOTALL)
lbs = []
for m in lb_pattern.finditer(src):
    lb_content = m.group(2)
    lbs.append({'pos': m.start(), 'len': len(lb_content), 'content': lb_content})
print(f'Found {len(lbs)} long brackets:')
for lb in lbs:
    print(f'  pos={lb["pos"]} len={lb["len"]} first50={repr(lb["content"][:50])}')

# Try ASCII85 on each long bracket
def decode_ascii85(data: str) -> bytes | None:
    """Standard ASCII85/base85 decode"""
    out = bytearray()
    i = 0
    s = data.encode('latin1')
    while i < len(s):
        b = s[i]
        if b == ord('z'):
            out.extend(b'\x00\x00\x00\x00')
            i += 1
            continue
        if b < 33 or b > 117:
            # Invalid char for base85
            if b in (32, 9, 10, 13):  # whitespace - skip
                i += 1; continue
            return None  # Invalid
        # Collect 5 chars
        group = []
        while i < len(s) and len(group) < 5:
            bb = s[i]
            if bb in (32, 9, 10, 13): i += 1; continue
            if bb < 33 or bb > 117: return None
            group.append(bb - 33)
            i += 1
        if len(group) == 0: break
        if len(group) < 5:
            # Pad
            pad = 5 - len(group)
            for _ in range(pad): group.append(84)
            val = 0
            for d in group:
                val = val * 85 + d
            # Only take (5-pad)*1 bytes? No: take 4-pad bytes
            full = [(val >> (8*(3-j))) & 0xFF for j in range(4)]
            out.extend(full[:4-pad+1])
        else:
            val = 0
            for d in group:
                val = val * 85 + d
            if val > 0xFFFFFFFF: return None
            out.extend([(val >> 24)&0xFF, (val>>16)&0xFF, (val>>8)&0xFF, val&0xFF])
    return bytes(out)

# Check if chars are in ASCII85 range
def check_ascii85_valid(data: str) -> tuple:
    s = data.encode('latin1')
    invalid = [chr(b) for b in s if b not in (32,9,10,13) and not (33 <= b <= 117) and b != ord('z')]
    return len(invalid) == 0, invalid[:5]

for lb in lbs:
    valid, inv = check_ascii85_valid(lb['content'])
    print(f'\nLB at pos={lb["pos"]} len={lb["len"]}:')
    print(f'  ASCII85 valid: {valid}', '' if valid else f'  invalid chars: {inv}')
    if valid:
        decoded = decode_ascii85(lb['content'])
        if decoded is not None:
            print(f'  Decoded: {len(decoded)} bytes')
            print(f'  First 32: {list(decoded[:32])}')
            print(f'  First 32 hex: {decoded[:32].hex()}')
            # Check for Lua magic
            if decoded[:4] == b'\x1bLua': print(f'  *** Lua 5.1 bytecode!')
            elif decoded[:4] == b'\x1bLuR': print(f'  *** Lua 5.2 bytecode!')
            # Save
            fname = f'/data/lb_{lb["pos"]}.bin'
            with open(fname, 'wb') as f: f.write(decoded)
            print(f'  Saved -> {fname}')
            # Check if first 4 bytes look like a count
            if len(decoded) >= 4:
                n = struct.unpack('<I', decoded[:4])[0]
                print(f'  First u32 LE: {n}')
                n2 = struct.unpack('>I', decoded[:4])[0]
                print(f'  First u32 BE: {n2}')
        else:
            print(f'  Decode failed (invalid sequence)')

# Also try the main payload from cleaned.lua
with open('/data/cleaned.lua','r',encoding='latin1') as f:
    cleaned = f.read()

# Find payload string
p = 31894
while cleaned[p] != '"': p += 1
payload_raw = []
i = p + 1
while i < len(cleaned):
    c = cleaned[i]
    if c == '\\':
        nc = cleaned[i+1]
        if nc == '\\': payload_raw.append(92); i += 2
        elif nc == '"': payload_raw.append(34); i += 2
        elif nc.isdigit():
            j = i+1
            while j < i+4 and cleaned[j].isdigit(): j += 1
            payload_raw.append(int(cleaned[i+1:j])); i = j
        else: payload_raw.append(ord(nc)); i += 2
    elif c == '"': break
    else: payload_raw.append(ord(c)); i += 1
payload_bytes = bytes(payload_raw)
print(f'\nMain payload: {len(payload_bytes)} bytes')

# Check if it's ASCII85
valid2, inv2 = check_ascii85_valid(payload_bytes.decode('latin1'))
print(f'ASCII85 valid: {valid2}', '' if valid2 else f'inv: {inv2}')
if valid2:
    decoded2 = decode_ascii85(payload_bytes.decode('latin1'))
    if decoded2:
        print(f'Decoded: {len(decoded2)} bytes')
        print(f'First 32 bytes: {list(decoded2[:32])}')
        print(f'First 32 hex: {decoded2[:32].hex()}')
        with open('/data/payload_a85.bin','wb') as f: f.write(decoded2)
        print('Saved -> /data/payload_a85.bin')

print('\n[done]')

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Full opcode tree traversal - binary tree dispatcher"""
import re, json

with open('/data/interpreter_section.lua','r',encoding='latin1') as f:
    src = f.read()
    lines = src.split('\n')

print(f'Interpreter: {len(lines)} lines')

# The dispatcher uses a binary tree on elem8
# Patterns:
# 1. if not (elem8 >= N) → elem8 < N branch
# 2. if elem8 < N → elem8 < N branch
# 3. if not (elem8 < N) → elem8 >= N branch
# 4. elseif elem8 == N → exact match
# 5. if elem8 >= N → branch

# Track ALL numeric comparisons with elem8
all_comparisons = []
for li, line in enumerate(lines):
    # Various forms
    m = re.search(r'elem8\s*([><=!]{1,3})\s*(\d+)', line)
    if m:
        all_comparisons.append({'line': li+1, 'op': m.group(1), 'val': int(m.group(2)), 'text': line.strip()})

print(f'Total elem8 comparisons: {len(all_comparisons)}')

# Find leaf opcode conditions (where code actually runs)
# A leaf is usually: if/elseif elem8 == N then ... (do something) ... end
# or the final else branch of a chain

# Extract all ==, >= sequences to build the range tree
leaf_ops = [(c['val'], c['line'], c['text']) for c in all_comparisons if c['op'] == '==']
boundary_ops = [(c['val'], c['line'], c['op'], c['text']) for c in all_comparisons if c['op'] in ('>=', '<', '<=', '>')]

print(f'Exact matches (==): {len(leaf_ops)}')
print(f'Boundary conditions (>=, <, etc): {len(boundary_ops)}')
print(f'\nLeaf opcodes: {sorted(set(v for v,_,_ in leaf_ops))}')

# For each leaf opcode, extract the code block (3 lines after)
leaf_semantics = {}
for val, li, text in leaf_ops:
    # Get lines after this one until next 'elseif'/'else'/'end'
    block = []
    for rel in range(1, 15):
        if li-1+rel >= len(lines): break
        l = lines[li-1+rel].strip()
        if not l: continue
        if l.startswith('elseif') or l == 'else' or l == 'end': break
        block.append(l)
        if len(block) >= 6: break
    leaf_semantics[val] = block

print('\n=== ALL LEAF OPCODE SEMANTICS ===')
for op in sorted(leaf_semantics.keys()):
    code = ' | '.join(leaf_semantics[op][:4])
    print(f'  OP {op:3d}: {code}')

# Map opcode to standard Lua instruction
op_map = {}
for op, block in leaf_semantics.items():
    code = ' '.join(block)
    if 'ret5' in code and '=' in code and 'ret5[' in code and 'ret5[' in code:
        # Register operations
        if '* ' in code or ' *' in code: op_map[op] = 'MUL'
        elif '+ ' in code and 'ret5' in code and '= ret5' in code: op_map[op] = 'ADD'
        elif '- ' in code and 'ret5' in code and '= ret5' in code: op_map[op] = 'SUB'
        elif '/ ' in code or ' /' in code: op_map[op] = 'DIV'
        elif '.. ' in code: op_map[op] = 'CONCAT'
        elif '>=' in code or '<=' in code or '==' in code or '~=' in code: op_map[op] = 'CMP'
        elif '[' in code and 'num9' in code and 'elem' in code: op_map[op] = 'LOADCONST'
    if 'num9 = ' in code: op_map[op] = 'JUMP'
    if 'k[' in code: op_map[op] = 'LOADK'
    if '= {}' in code: op_map[op] = 'NEWTABLE'

print('\n=== INSTRUCTION TYPE MAP ===')
for op in sorted(op_map.keys()):
    print(f'  OP {op:3d}: {op_map[op]}')

# Save results
with open('/data/opcode_full.json','w') as f:
    json.dump({'leaf_ops': leaf_semantics, 'type_map': op_map}, f, indent=2)
print('\nSaved opcode_full.json')

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Parse lb_82937.bin - try to find proto structure"""
import struct, json

with open('/data/lb_82937.bin','rb') as f:
    data = f.read()
print(f'Data: {len(data)} bytes')
print(f'First 64 bytes: {list(data[:64])}')
print(f'First 64 hex: {data[:64].hex()}')

# Count byte frequencies
from collections import Counter
byte_freq = Counter(data)
print(f'\nMost common bytes: {byte_freq.most_common(10)}')
print(f'Least common bytes: {byte_freq.most_common()[-10:]}')
print(f'Unique byte values: {len(byte_freq)}')

# Check if it looks like integers (many 0x00 bytes if u32)
n_zeros = byte_freq.get(0, 0)
print(f'Zero bytes: {n_zeros} ({100*n_zeros/len(data):.1f}%)')

# XOR with the 9-uint32 key
xor_key_u32 = [1516, 2592322951, 3870559914, 1506747566, 3016141655, 2023543291, 3577965033, 741229669, 634733336]
xor_key = bytearray()
for k in xor_key_u32:
    xor_key.extend(struct.pack('<I', k))
print(f'\nXOR key: {list(xor_key[:16])}...')

xored = bytes([b ^ xor_key[i % len(xor_key)] for i,b in enumerate(data)])
print(f'XOR decoded first 32: {list(xored[:32])}')
print(f'XOR decoded first 32 hex: {xored[:32].hex()}')

# Check for Lua magic after XOR
if xored[:4] == b'\x1bLua': print('*** Lua 5.1/5.2 bytecode after XOR!')
if xored[:4] == b'\x1bLuR': print('*** Lua 5.2 bytecode after XOR!')

# Try parsing as varint stream (Lua-style)
def read_varint(data, pos):
    """Luraph uses a simple varint: bytes b1,b2,... where each has 7 bits of data, MSB=1 means more bytes"""
    val = 0
    shift = 0
    while True:
        if pos >= len(data): return None, pos
        b = data[pos]; pos += 1
        val |= (b & 0x7F) << shift
        shift += 7
        if not (b & 0x80): break
    return val, pos

# Try varint on raw data
print('\nVarint parse (raw):')
pos = 0
vals = []
for _ in range(30):
    v, pos = read_varint(data, pos)
    if v is None: break
    vals.append(v)
print(f'First 30 varints: {vals}')

# Try varint on XOR decoded data  
print('\nVarint parse (XOR decoded):')
pos = 0
vals2 = []
for _ in range(30):
    v, pos = read_varint(xored, pos)
    if v is None: break
    vals2.append(v)
print(f'First 30 varints: {vals2}')

# Try simple byte array interpretation
print('\nRaw bytes as values, first 50:', list(data[:50]))
print('XOR bytes as values, first 50:', list(xored[:50]))

# Try: data = packed instructions, each 4 bytes LE
print('\n=== u32 LE parse (raw) ===')
ints = [struct.unpack_from('<I', data, i)[0] for i in range(0, min(80, len(data)), 4)]
print(f'First 20 u32: {ints[:20]}')

print('\n=== u32 LE parse (XOR) ===')
ints_x = [struct.unpack_from('<I', xored, i)[0] for i in range(0, min(80, len(xored)), 4)]
print(f'First 20 u32: {ints_x[:20]}')

# Check if first value looks like a proto count
for label, arr in [('raw', ints), ('xor', ints_x)]:
    n = arr[0]
    if 1 <= n <= 500:
        print(f'\n{label}: first u32={n} looks like proto count!')
        # Try to parse: each proto = instruction_count + instruction_data
        idx = 1
        for pn in range(min(n, 10)):
            if idx >= len(arr): break
            ni = arr[idx]; idx += 1
            if ni > 10000: print(f'  Proto {pn}: instruction count {ni} too large, stopping'); break
            instrs = arr[idx:idx+ni]; idx += ni
            print(f'  Proto {pn}: {ni} instructions, first 5: {instrs[:5]}')

# Try: data as byte pairs → 16-bit values
print('\n=== u16 LE parse (first 40) ===')
u16s = [struct.unpack_from('<H', data, i)[0] for i in range(0, min(80, len(data)), 2)]
print(u16s[:40])

print('[done]')

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Mega parser - try every approach on lb_82937.bin and the payload"""
import struct, json, re, os

with open('/data/lb_82937.bin','rb') as f:
    data = f.read()
print(f'=== lb_82937.bin: {len(data)} bytes ===')

# --- 1) Find structure by looking for repeating small counts ---
print('\n--- Looking for size headers ---')
# Common pattern: N-byte count + N-byte data
for offset in range(0, 20):
    b1 = data[offset]
    # Try: byte b1 = count, then b1 bytes of data
    if 1 <= b1 <= 100:
        rest = data[offset+1:offset+1+b1]
        print(f'  offset={offset}: byte={b1}, next {b1} bytes: {list(rest[:10])}')

# --- 2) Try parse as Luraph proto dump ---
# Format hypothesis: each proto = { nparams, nupvals, ninstrs, [instrs], nconsts, [consts], nprotos, [protos] }
# where integers are encoded as individual bytes OR u32 LE

def try_parse_protos_bytes(data, pos=0, depth=0):
    """Try to parse as byte-encoded proto array"""
    if pos >= len(data): return None, pos
    n_instrs = data[pos]; pos += 1
    if n_instrs > 200: return None, pos
    if pos + n_instrs > len(data): return None, pos
    
    # Read instructions (each is an opcode byte?)
    instrs = list(data[pos:pos+n_instrs]); pos += n_instrs
    
    # Read constants
    if pos >= len(data): return None, pos
    n_consts = data[pos]; pos += 1
    consts = []
    for _ in range(n_consts):
        if pos >= len(data): return None, pos
        ctype = data[pos]; pos += 1
        if ctype == 0:  # nil
            consts.append(None)
        elif ctype == 1:  # bool  
            if pos >= len(data): return None, pos
            consts.append(bool(data[pos])); pos += 1
        elif ctype == 3:  # number (8 bytes float64)
            if pos + 8 > len(data): return None, pos
            v = struct.unpack_from('<d', data, pos)[0]; pos += 8
            consts.append(v)
        elif ctype == 4:  # string (u32 len + bytes)
            if pos + 4 > len(data): return None, pos
            slen = struct.unpack_from('<I', data, pos)[0]; pos += 4
            if pos + slen > len(data): return None, pos
            s = data[pos:pos+slen].decode('latin1', errors='replace'); pos += slen
            consts.append(s)
        else:
            return None, pos  # Unknown type
    
    # Read sub-protos
    if pos >= len(data): return None, pos
    n_subs = data[pos]; pos += 1
    subs = []
    for _ in range(n_subs):
        sub, pos = try_parse_protos_bytes(data, pos, depth+1)
        if sub is None: return None, pos
        subs.append(sub)
    
    return {'n_instrs': n_instrs, 'instrs': instrs, 'consts': consts, 'subs': subs}, pos

print('\n--- Try parse_protos_bytes from offset 0 ---')
result, end_pos = try_parse_protos_bytes(data, 0)
if result:
    print(f'SUCCESS at byte offset! End pos: {end_pos}')
    print(f'Root proto: {result["n_instrs"]} instrs, {len(result["consts"])} consts, {len(result["subs"])} subs')
else:
    print(f'Failed at pos {end_pos}')

# --- 3) Try parse with u32 sizes ---
def try_parse_protos_u32(data, pos=0, depth=0):
    """Try to parse as u32 LE count proto array"""
    if pos + 4 > len(data): return None, pos
    n_instrs = struct.unpack_from('<I', data, pos)[0]; pos += 4
    if n_instrs > 50000: return None, pos
    if pos + n_instrs*4 > len(data): return None, pos
    
    instrs = [struct.unpack_from('<I', data, i*4+pos)[0] for i in range(n_instrs)]
    pos += n_instrs * 4
    
    if pos + 4 > len(data): return None, pos
    n_consts = struct.unpack_from('<I', data, pos)[0]; pos += 4
    if n_consts > 10000: return None, pos
    
    return {'n_instrs': n_instrs, 'instrs': instrs[:5], 'n_consts': n_consts}, pos

print('\n--- Try parse_protos_u32 from offset 0 ---')
result2, end_pos2 = try_parse_protos_u32(data, 0)
if result2:
    print(f'SUCCESS at u32! n_instrs={result2["n_instrs"]}, n_consts={result2["n_consts"]}, end={end_pos2}')
    print(f'First 5 instrs: {result2["instrs"]}')
else:
    print(f'Failed at pos {end_pos2}')

# --- 4) Extract the ORIGINAL source section at 116370-138283 ---
with open('/data/target.lua','r',encoding='latin1') as f:
    orig = f.read()
print(f'\n=== Original source excerpt (116370-138283) ===')
print(f'Total original: {len(orig)} chars')
excerpt = orig[116370:138283]
print(f'Excerpt: {len(excerpt)} chars')
print(f'First 300 chars: {repr(excerpt[:300])}')

# --- 5) Try ALL possible offsets for varint parse ---
print('\n--- Varint parse at different offsets ---')
def read_varint(data, pos):
    val = 0; shift = 0
    while True:
        if pos >= len(data): return None, pos
        b = data[pos]; pos += 1
        val |= (b & 0x7F) << shift; shift += 7
        if not (b & 0x80): break
    return val, pos

for start in range(0, 5):
    pos = start
    vals = []
    for _ in range(20):
        v, pos = read_varint(data, pos)
        if v is None: break
        vals.append(v)
    print(f'  offset={start}: {vals}')

# --- 6) Parse as ZIG-ZAG encoded varints ---
def zigzag_decode(n):
    return (n >> 1) ^ -(n & 1)

pos = 0; vals_zz = []
for _ in range(30):
    v, pos = read_varint(data, pos)
    if v is None: break
    vals_zz.append(zigzag_decode(v))
print(f'\nZigZag varints: {vals_zz[:30]}')

# --- 7) Look at the original source structure to understand what k() receives ---
# Find the CALL to k() in the original source
k_call = orig.find('k(')
if k_call != -1:
    print(f'\n=== k() call in original at pos {k_call} ===')
    print(repr(orig[max(0,k_call-50):k_call+200]))

# Find ALL calls to k(
# and also find where the XOR key is defined
xor_pos = orig.find('1516')
if xor_pos != -1:
    print(f'\n=== XOR key area (1516) at pos {xor_pos} ===')
    print(repr(orig[max(0,xor_pos-100):xor_pos+200]))

print('\n[done]')
