#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Decode the actual [=[...]=] payload from target.lua"""
import re, struct, json

with open('/data/target.lua','r',encoding='latin1') as f:
    orig = f.read()
print(f'Original: {len(orig)} chars')

# Find [=[...]=] long bracket (level 1)
# This is the actual payload
pattern_l1 = re.compile(r'\[=(\[)(.*?)\]=(\])', re.DOTALL)
m = pattern_l1.search(orig)
if m:
    payload_raw = m.group(2)
    print(f'Found [=[...]=] at pos {m.start()}, content len={len(payload_raw)}')
    print(f'First 80 chars: {repr(payload_raw[:80])}')
else:
    print('No [=[...]=] found!')
    # Try level 2: [==[ ]==]
    pattern_l2 = re.compile(r'\[==(\[)(.*?)\]==(\])', re.DOTALL)
    m2 = pattern_l2.search(orig)
    if m2:
        payload_raw = m2.group(2)
        print(f'Found [==[...]==] at pos {m2.start()}, content len={len(payload_raw)}')
    else:
        print('No level-2 LB either!')
        payload_raw = None

if payload_raw is None:
    exit(1)

# Try ASCII85 decode on the full payload
print(f'\nPayload range: {min(ord(c) for c in payload_raw)}-{max(ord(c) for c in payload_raw)}')

# Check all chars are valid ASCII85 (33-117 or z=122)
invalid = [(i,c) for i,c in enumerate(payload_raw) if not (33 <= ord(c) <= 117 or ord(c) == 122)]
if invalid:
    print(f'Invalid chars for ASCII85: {invalid[:10]}')
    # What ARE the invalid chars?
    uniq_invalid = set(ord(c) for _,c in invalid)
    print(f'Unique invalid byte values: {sorted(uniq_invalid)}')
else:
    print('All chars valid for ASCII85!')

# ASCII85 decode
def ascii85_decode(data):
    out = bytearray()
    i = 0
    while i < len(data):
        b = ord(data[i]) if isinstance(data[i], str) else data[i]
        if b == 122:  # 'z' = 4 zero bytes
            out.extend(b'\x00\x00\x00\x00')
            i += 1
            continue
        if b in (32, 9, 10, 13):
            i += 1; continue
        # Collect group of 5
        group = []
        while i < len(data) and len(group) < 5:
            bb = ord(data[i]) if isinstance(data[i], str) else data[i]
            if bb in (32, 9, 10, 13): i += 1; continue
            if bb < 33 or bb > 117: return None, f'invalid byte {bb} at pos {i}'
            group.append(bb - 33)
            i += 1
        if len(group) == 0: break
        if len(group) < 5:
            # Last partial group: pad with 'u' (84)
            pad = 5 - len(group)
            for _ in range(pad): group.append(84)
            val = 0
            for d in group: val = val * 85 + d
            # Take 4-pad bytes
            full = [(val >> (8*(3-j))) & 0xFF for j in range(4)]
            out.extend(full[:4-pad])
        else:
            val = 0
            for d in group: val = val * 85 + d
            if val > 0xFFFFFFFF: return None, f'overflow {val}'
            out.extend([(val>>24)&0xFF, (val>>16)&0xFF, (val>>8)&0xFF, val&0xFF])
    return bytes(out), None

decoded, err = ascii85_decode(payload_raw)
if err:
    print(f'Decode error: {err}')
    # Find more details
    for i, c in enumerate(payload_raw):
        b = ord(c)
        if b < 33 or (b > 117 and b != 122):
            print(f'  First invalid at pos {i}: chr={repr(c)} byte={b}')
            break
else:
    print(f'Decoded: {len(decoded)} bytes!')
    print(f'First 32 bytes: {list(decoded[:32])}')
    print(f'First 32 hex: {decoded[:32].hex()}')
    with open('/data/payload_full.bin', 'wb') as f:
        f.write(decoded)
    print(f'Saved -> /data/payload_full.bin')
    
    # XOR decode with key
    xor_u32 = [1516, 2592322951, 3870559914, 1506747566, 3016141655, 2023543291, 3577965033, 741229669, 634733336]
    xor_key = bytearray()
    for k in xor_u32:
        xor_key.extend(struct.pack('<I', k))
    
    xored = bytes([b ^ xor_key[i % len(xor_key)] for i,b in enumerate(decoded)])
    print(f'XOR decoded first 32: {list(xored[:32])}')
    print(f'XOR decoded first 32 hex: {xored[:32].hex()}')
    with open('/data/payload_xor.bin', 'wb') as f:
        f.write(xored)
    print(f'Saved -> /data/payload_xor.bin')
    
    # Check for Lua magic bytes
    if xored[:4] == b'\x1bLua': print('*** Standard Lua 5.1 bytecode after XOR!')
    if xored[:4] == b'\x1bLuR': print('*** Lua 5.2 bytecode after XOR!')
    
    # Parse as varint stream
    def read_varint(data, pos):
        val = 0; shift = 0
        while pos < len(data):
            b = data[pos]; pos += 1
            val |= (b & 0x7F) << shift; shift += 7
            if not (b & 0x80): break
        return val, pos
    
    print('\nVarint parse (raw decoded):')
    pos = 0; vals = []
    for _ in range(30):
        v, pos = read_varint(decoded, pos)
        vals.append(v)
    print(f'  {vals}')
    
    print('\nVarint parse (XOR decoded):')
    pos = 0; vals2 = []
    for _ in range(30):
        v, pos = read_varint(xored, pos)
        vals2.append(v)
    print(f'  {vals2}')

print('\n[done]')

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Decode Luraph payload - base-89 with 'd' separator analysis"""
import re, struct, json

with open('/data/target.lua','r',encoding='latin1') as f:
    orig = f.read()

# Extract [=[...]=] payload
m = re.search(r'\[=(\[)(.*?)\]=(\])', orig, re.DOTALL)
payload = m.group(2)
print(f'Payload: {len(payload)} chars')

# Step 1: Verify the 'd' separator pattern
print('\n=== SEPARATOR ANALYSIS ===')
payload_bytes = [ord(c) for c in payload]

# Count: how many 'd'=100 appear at every-5th vs other positions?
sep_positions = [i for i,b in enumerate(payload_bytes) if b == 100]
non_sep_dcount = [p for p in sep_positions if p % 5 != 4]
every5_dcount = [p for p in sep_positions if p % 5 == 4]
print(f'Total d=100 occurrences: {len(sep_positions)}')
print(f'd at every-5th (pos 4,9,14...): {len(every5_dcount)}')
print(f'd at non-5th positions: {len(non_sep_dcount)}')
print(f'Missing d at some 5th positions: {91659//5 - len(every5_dcount)}')

# Check total groups
print(f'Expected groups (91659/5): {91659/5:.1f}')

# Step 2: Confirm all 5th-position chars are 'd'
all_5th = [payload_bytes[i] for i in range(4, len(payload_bytes), 5)]
not_d = [(i*5+4, all_5th[i]) for i in range(len(all_5th)) if all_5th[i] != 100]
print(f'Non-d chars at 5th positions: {len(not_d)} (first few: {not_d[:5]})')

# Step 3: Extract groups of 4 data bytes
groups = []
for i in range(0, len(payload_bytes)-4, 5):
    sep = payload_bytes[i+4]
    if sep != 100:
        print(f'WARNING: group {i//5} has sep={sep} not d at pos {i+4}')
    group = payload_bytes[i:i+4]
    groups.append(group)
print(f'Total groups: {len(groups)}')

# Step 4: Decode each group - try treating bytes as individual values
# Value mapping: char-33, skipping 100 (gap at 67 in shifted space)
def decode_val(b):
    """Map char to value 0-88, skipping separator value 67"""
    v = b - 33
    if v >= 67: v -= 1  # skip the gap at 67
    return v  # range 0-88

# Check first 20 groups
print('\n=== FIRST 20 GROUPS ===')
for i, g in enumerate(groups[:20]):
    vals = [decode_val(b) for b in g]
    raw = [b-33 for b in g]  # raw shifted
    print(f'  Group {i:3d}: chars={[chr(b) for b in g]} raw={raw} vals={vals}')

# Step 5: Try opcode hypothesis - first val = opcode
print('\n=== OPCODE DISTRIBUTION (first val of each group) ===')
from collections import Counter
op_vals = [decode_val(g[0]) for g in groups]
op_counter = Counter(op_vals)
print(f'Most common first values: {op_counter.most_common(20)}')
print(f'First value range: {min(op_vals)}-{max(op_vals)}')

# Known opcodes from cleaned interpreter
known_ops = {1,4,7,15,18,21,32,37,43,48,54,59,67,70,73,76,78,81,87,92,95,103,109,117,125,144,147,150,158,167,170,173}
known_in_data = known_ops.intersection(set(op_vals))
print(f'Known opcodes appearing as first val: {sorted(known_in_data)}')
print(f'({len(known_in_data)}/{len(known_ops)} known ops appear in data)')

# Step 6: Try base-89 LE decode of all 4 values → one instruction word
print('\n=== BASE-89 DECODE (4 vals → one u32) ===')
def decode_b89(g):
    vals = [decode_val(b) for b in g]
    return vals[0] + vals[1]*89 + vals[2]*89**2 + vals[3]*89**3

words = [decode_b89(g) for g in groups]
print(f'First 20 words: {words[:20]}')
print(f'Word range: {min(words)}-{max(words)}')

# If opcode is in lowest 8 bits of base-89 word:
ops_from_word = [w & 0xFF for w in words]
op_ctr2 = Counter(ops_from_word)
print(f'\nOps from word lowest 8 bits, top 20: {op_ctr2.most_common(20)}')
known_in_word = known_ops.intersection(set(ops_from_word))
print(f'Known ops appearing: {sorted(known_in_word)} ({len(known_in_word)}/{len(known_ops)})')

# If opcode is bits 7-0 of base-89 word:
# Field layout hypothesis: [opcode:8, A:8, B:8]
print('\n=== INSTRUCTION FIELDS FROM BASE-89 WORD ===')
for i, w in enumerate(words[:15]):
    op = w & 0xFF
    fA = (w >> 8) & 0xFF
    fB = (w >> 16) & 0xFF
    print(f'  instr {i:3d}: word=0x{w:06X} op={op:3d} A={fA} B={fB}')

# Step 7: Reconstruct proto arrays using word-based decode
# Hypothesis: words[0] = n_protos, words[1..] = instruction data
print(f'\nwords[0] = {words[0]} (proto count?)')
if words[0] < 100:
    print(f'Looks like proto count!')
    n_protos = words[0]
    pos = 1
    for pn in range(min(n_protos, 10)):
        if pos >= len(words): break
        n_instrs = words[pos]; pos += 1
        if n_instrs > 20000: print(f'  Proto {pn}: instr count {n_instrs} too large'); break
        instrs = words[pos:pos+n_instrs]; pos += n_instrs
        print(f'  Proto {pn}: {n_instrs} instrs, first 5 ops: {[w & 0xFF for w in instrs[:5]]}')

# Save groups for further analysis
with open('/data/groups.json','w') as f:
    json.dump({'groups': [[b for b in g] for g in groups[:100]], 'words': words[:100]}, f)
print('\nSaved groups.json')
print('[done]')

    b = ord(payload_str[i])
    if b == 122:
        i += 1; group_num += 1; continue
    grp = []
    start_i = i
    while i < len(payload_str) and len(grp) < 5:
        bb = ord(payload_str[i])
        if bb > 117 and bb != 122:
            print(f'  First invalid char at pos {i}: chr={repr(payload_str[i])} byte={bb} in group {group_num}')
            # What are the chars in this group?
            print(f'  Group start at {start_i}: chars={[repr(payload_str[j]) for j in range(start_i, min(start_i+5, len(payload_str)))]}')
            break
        grp.append(bb-33)
        i += 1
    else:
        if len(grp) == 5:
            val = 0
            for d in grp: val = val*85+d
            if val > 0xFFFFFFFF:
                print(f'  Overflow at group {group_num} pos {start_i}: val={val}')
                print(f'  Group chars: {[repr(payload_str[j]) for j in range(start_i, start_i+5)]}')
                print(f'  Group vals: {grp}')
                break
        group_num += 1
        continue
    break

print('[done]')

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""FINAL decoder: ASCII85 BE + mod 2^32, skip 4-char header, z-expansion, then XOR key"""
import re, struct, json

with open('/data/target.lua', 'r', encoding='latin1') as f:
    orig = f.read()

# Extract payload from [=[...]=]
m = re.search(r'\[=(\[)(.*?)\]=(\])', orig, re.DOTALL)
payload_str = m.group(2)
print(f'Raw payload: {len(payload_str)} chars')
print(f'Header (first 4 chars): {repr(payload_str[:4])}')
print(f"'z' count in payload: {payload_str.count(chr(122))}")
print(f"'z' in first 4: {chr(122) in payload_str[:4]}")

# Step 1: Expand 'z' -> '!!!!!' ONLY in the data portion (after first 4 chars)
header = payload_str[:4]
data_raw = payload_str[4:]
data_expanded = data_raw.replace(chr(122), '!!!!!')

print(f'Data after header: {len(data_raw)} chars')
print(f"z in data: {data_raw.count(chr(122))}")
print(f'Data after z-expansion: {len(data_expanded)} chars')

# Step 2: Decode in groups of 5 using ASCII85 BE formula, mod 2^32
output = bytearray()
overflow_count = 0
for i in range(0, len(data_expanded) - len(data_expanded) % 5, 5):
    c = [ord(data_expanded[i+j]) - 33 for j in range(5)]
    # Validate all digits are in [0, 84]
    if any(d < 0 or d > 84 for d in c):
        print(f'Invalid digits at group {i//5}: {c} chars={[repr(data_expanded[i+j]) for j in range(5)]}')
        continue
    W = c[0]*52200625 + c[1]*614125 + c[2]*7225 + c[3]*85 + c[4]
    if W > 0xFFFFFFFF:
        overflow_count += 1
        W = W & 0xFFFFFFFF  # mod 2^32 (matches Lua bit32 behavior)
    output.extend([(W>>24)&0xFF, (W>>16)&0xFF, (W>>8)&0xFF, W&0xFF])

print(f'\nDecoded (before XOR): {len(output)} bytes')
print(f'Overflow groups: {overflow_count}')
print(f'First 32 bytes hex: {output[:32].hex()}')

# Step 3: Apply XOR with the key _={1516,...}
xor_u32 = [1516, 2592322951, 3870559914, 1506747566, 3016141655, 2023543291, 3577965033, 741229669, 634733336]
key = bytearray()
for k in xor_u32:
    key.extend(struct.pack('<I', k))
print(f'XOR key (36 bytes): {key.hex()}')

xored = bytes([b ^ key[i % len(key)] for i, b in enumerate(output)])
print(f'\nAfter XOR: {len(xored)} bytes')
print(f'First 32 hex: {xored[:32].hex()}')
print(f'Byte range: {min(xored)}-{max(xored)}')

# Check for known Luraph proto magic
for offset in range(0, min(64, len(xored))):
    b = xored[offset]
    if b == 0x1B:  # Lua magic
        print(f'Possible Lua magic at offset {offset}: {xored[offset:offset+8].hex()}')

# Try varint parse at offset 0
def rv(data, pos):
    v=0; s=0
    while pos < len(data):
        b = data[pos]; pos += 1
        v |= (b & 0x7F) << s; s += 7
        if not (b & 0x80): break
    return v, pos

print('\nVarint stream from offset 0:')
pos=0; vals=[]
for _ in range(20):
    v, pos = rv(xored, pos)
    vals.append(v)
print(f'{vals}')

# Check if first byte could be a proto header
print(f'\nFirst byte: {xored[0]} (0x{xored[0]:02X})')
print(f'First 8 bytes: {list(xored[:8])}')

# Save the decoded data
with open('/data/decoded_payload.bin', 'wb') as f:
    f.write(xored)
print(f'\nSaved to /data/decoded_payload.bin')

# Try different XOR key orderings (maybe key is applied differently)
# Check if header bytes encode something
header_vals = [ord(c)-33 for c in header]
header_w = header_vals[0]*614125 + header_vals[1]*7225 + header_vals[2]*85 + header_vals[3]
print(f'\nHeader chars: {repr(header)}')
print(f'Header vals: {header_vals}')
print(f'Header as 24-bit word (3 high digits): {header_w}')
print(f'Header first 3 as b85: {header_vals[0]*7225 + header_vals[1]*85 + header_vals[2]}')

# Try: header bytes = size of output
print(f'Header as 4-byte BE: {struct.pack(">BBBB", *[ord(c) for c in header]).hex()}')
# Skip 4 chars header might be: magic or expected output size
# output size = 73324 = 0x11EBC
print(f'Expected output size: {len(output)} = 0x{len(output):X}')

# Try XOR then parse as Luraph proto stream
# Luraph proto: each proto is a sequence of integers
# First value = number of sub-protos
# Try parsing as simple byte stream of LEB128 values
print('\n=== Try Luraph-like proto parse ===')
# In Luraph bytecode, the stream starts with version/header
# Look for repeating patterns
from collections import Counter
byte_freq = Counter(xored)
print(f'Most common bytes: {byte_freq.most_common(20)}')

# Check if the data looks like it has a header
# Many Luraph variants start with specific header bytes
for test_key_start in [0, 4, 8, 16, 32]:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Full Luraph disassembler for decoded_payload.bin"""
import struct, json, os
from collections import Counter, defaultdict

with open('/data/decoded_payload.bin','rb') as f:
    data = bytearray(f.read())

print('=== LURAPH FULL DISASSEMBLER ===')
print(f'Binary size: {len(data)} bytes')

# ---- HEADER (5 LEB128 fields, 7 bytes) ----
def read_leb128(data, pos):
    val, shift = 0, 0
    while pos < len(data):
        b = data[pos]; pos += 1
        val |= (b & 0x7F) << shift; shift += 7
        if not (b & 0x80): break
    return val, pos

pos = 0
header = []
for _ in range(5):
    v, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
    header.append(v)

numSubProtos, numParams, maxStack, numInstrs, numConsts = header
print(f'\nMAIN PROTO HEADER:')
print(f'  numSubProtos={numSubProtos}, numParams={numParams}, maxStack={maxStack}')
print(f'  numInstrs={numInstrs}, numConsts={numConsts}')
print(f'  Instructions start at byte {pos} ({numInstrs}x4={numInstrs*4} bytes)')

# ---- INSTRUCTIONS ----
instr_start = pos
instrs = []
for i in range(numInstrs):
    bp = instr_start + i*4
    A, B, C, D = data[bp], data[bp+1], data[bp+2], data[bp+3]
    opcode = B >> 3
    S = B & 7
    K = C >> 3
    x = C & 7
    U = D >> 3
    d = D & 7
    instrs.append((opcode, S, K, x, U, d, A))

const_start = instr_start + numInstrs * 4
print(f'  Constants start at byte {const_start}')

# ---- CONSTANTS ----
pos = const_start
consts = []
for _ in range(numConsts):
    v, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
    consts.append(v)

subproto_start = pos
print(f'  Sub-protos start at byte {pos} ({len(data)-pos} bytes remaining)')

print(f'\n=== OPCODE STATISTICS ===')
op_counts = Counter(i[0] for i in instrs)
print('Opcode distribution (sorted by count):')
for op, cnt in sorted(op_counts.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1]):
    pct = 100*cnt/numInstrs
    print(f'  op{op:2d}: {cnt:5d} ({pct:4.1f}%)')

print(f'\n=== FIELD ANALYSIS PER OPCODE ===')
op_data = defaultdict(lambda: {'K':[], 'U':[], 'A':[], 'S':[], 'x':[], 'd':[]})
for op, S, K, x, U, d, A in instrs:
    op_data[op]['K'].append(K)
    op_data[op]['U'].append(U)
    op_data[op]['A'].append(A)
    op_data[op]['S'].append(S)
    op_data[op]['x'].append(x)
    op_data[op]['d'].append(d)

for op in sorted(op_data.keys()):
    d = op_data[op]
    K_vals = set(d['K'])
    U_vals = set(d['U'])
    A_vals = set(d['A'])
    K_range = (min(d['K']), max(d['K']))
    U_range = (min(d['U']), max(d['U']))
    A_range = (min(d['A']), max(d['A']))
    # Try to identify opcode type:
    is_const_ref = K_range[1] > 24  # references multiple constants
    is_reg_only = A_range[1] <= 77  # only register indices
    print(f'  op{op:2d}: count={op_counts[op]:4d} K=[{K_range[0]},{K_range[1]}] U=[{U_range[0]},{U_range[1]}] A=[{A_range[0]},{A_range[1]}] S_vals={set(d["S"])} unique_K={len(K_vals)}')

print(f'\n=== CONSTANT ANALYSIS ===')
print(f'Total constants: {len(consts)}')
# Try float64 bit-cast
float_like = []
string_like = []
int_like = []
for i, v in enumerate(consts):
    if v < 2**64:
        try:
            f = struct.unpack('<d', struct.pack('<Q', v))[0]
            if 0.001 < abs(f) < 1e12 and f == f and f != float('inf'):
                float_like.append((i, v, f))
        except: pass
    if v < 10471: int_like.append((i,v))  # could be an index into const table itself
    if 0 < v < 128: string_like.append((i,v))  # ASCII char

print(f'Float-like constants (bit-cast float64): {len(float_like)} / {numConsts}')
for i,v,f in float_like[:20]:
    print(f'  [{i:5d}] {v} -> float64={f:.6g}')

print(f'\nSmall (<128) constants (ASCII?): {len(string_like)} / {numConsts}')
print('Distribution:', Counter(v for _,v in string_like).most_common(20))

print(f'\nSelf-referencing constants (< {numConsts}): {len(int_like)}')

# Check if large values are float bit-casts for specific float ranges
print(f'\nChecking specific large constants as float64:')
for i in [34, 59, 100, 200, 500, 1000]:
    if i < len(consts):
        v = consts[i]
        if v < 2**64:
            try:
                f = struct.unpack('<d', struct.pack('<Q', v))[0]
                print(f'  [{i}] {v} -> float64={f:.10g}')
            except: pass

print(f'\n=== INSTRUCTION STREAM (first 100 instructions) ===')
op_names = {i: f'op{i:02d}' for i in range(32)}
print(f'{"IDX":>5} {"OP":>5} {"S":>3} {"K":>3} {"x":>3} {"U":>3} {"d":>3} {"A":>5} | CONST_K')
for i in range(min(100, numInstrs)):
    op, S, K, x, U, d, A = instrs[i]
    cval = consts[K] if K < len(consts) else '?'
    print(f'{i:5d} {op_names[op]:>5} {S:3d} {K:3d} {x:3d} {U:3d} {d:3d} {A:5d} | [{K}]={cval}')

print(f'\n=== INSTRUCTION STREAM (around entry PC=40) ===')
print(f'{"IDX":>5} {"OP":>5} {"S":>3} {"K":>3} {"x":>3} {"U":>3} {"d":>3} {"A":>5} | CONST_K')
for i in range(35, min(60, numInstrs)):
    op, S, K, x, U, d, A = instrs[i]
    cval = consts[K] if K < len(consts) else '?'
    marker = ' <-- ENTRY' if i==40 else ''
    print(f'{i:5d} {op_names[op]:>5} {S:3d} {K:3d} {x:3d} {U:3d} {d:3d} {A:5d} | [{K}]={cval}{marker}')

# Save full disassembly
with open('/data/full_disasm.json','w') as f:
    json.dump({'header': header, 'instrs': instrs, 'consts': consts,
               'instr_start': instr_start, 'const_start': const_start,
               'subproto_start': subproto_start}, f)

print(f'\nFull disassembly saved to /data/full_disasm.json')
print(f'({len(instrs)} instructions, {len(consts)} constants)')

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Deep semantic analysis to identify opcode meanings"""
import json, struct
from collections import Counter, defaultdict

with open('/data/full_disasm.json') as f:
    d = json.load(f)

instrs = d['instrs']  # each: [opcode, S, K, x, U, d, A]
consts = d['consts']
numInstrs = len(instrs)

# Helper: compute combined byte values
def KX(instr): return instr[2]*8 + instr[3]   # K*8 + x (8-bit)
def UD(instr): return instr[4]*8 + instr[5]   # U*8 + d (8-bit)
def AA(instr): return instr[6]                 # A byte (8-bit)
def full16(instr): return KX(instr)*256 + UD(instr)  # 16-bit

print('=== SEMANTIC ANALYSIS ===')

# 1. Find RETURN-like instructions
# RETURN usually appears at end of functions or near JMP targets
# Look for instructions that could be RETURN by analyzing context
print('\n1. LAST 20 INSTRUCTIONS (likely RETURN at end):')
for i in range(max(0,numInstrs-20), numInstrs):
    op,S,K,x,U,d,A = instrs[i]
    print(f'  [{i:5d}] op{op:02d} S={S} K={K} x={x} U={U} d={d} A={A}')

# 2. Analyze field distributions for identifying LOADK
# LOADK: should reference a wide range of constants (high variety in const index field)
# The 'const_index' field would use 10471 values, so the COMBINED field encoding it
# should have high entropy
print('\n2. Const index encoding analysis:')
for op in sorted(set(i[0] for i in instrs)):
    op_instrs = [i for i in instrs if i[0]==op]
    # Try different field combinations as const index
    kx_vals = set(KX(i) for i in op_instrs)
    ud_vals = set(UD(i) for i in op_instrs)
    a_vals = set(AA(i) for i in op_instrs)
    full16_vals = set(full16(i) for i in op_instrs)
    a_kx_vals = set(AA(i)*256+KX(i) for i in op_instrs)
    kx_ud_vals = set(KX(i)*256+UD(i) for i in op_instrs)  # = full16
    # Also try KX-based const reference
    # Measure entropy (number of unique values relative to count)
    entropy_full16 = len(full16_vals)
    entropy_a_kx = len(a_kx_vals)
    if op in [29,21,31,10,3,12,16]:  # top opcodes
        print(f'  op{op:02d}: unique(KX)={len(kx_vals):3d}, unique(UD)={len(ud_vals):3d}, unique(A)={len(a_vals):3d}, unique(full16)={entropy_full16:5d}, unique(A<<8|KX)={entropy_a_kx:5d}')

print('  ...')
for op in sorted(set(i[0] for i in instrs)):
    op_instrs = [i for i in instrs if i[0]==op]
    full16_vals = set(full16(i) for i in op_instrs)
    a_kx_vals = set(AA(i)*256+KX(i) for i in op_instrs)
    kx_a_vals = set(KX(i)*256+AA(i) for i in op_instrs)
    print(f'  op{op:02d}: cnt={len(op_instrs):4d} uniq_full16={len(full16_vals):5d} uniq_A|KX={len(a_kx_vals):5d} uniq_KX|A={len(kx_a_vals):5d}')

# 3. Look for string constants by finding ASCII runs in const table
print('\n3. String detection - runs of printable ASCII in const table:')
printable = [c for c in range(32,127)]
current_run = []
runs = []
for i, v in enumerate(consts):
    if 32 <= v <= 126:
        current_run.append((i, v))
    else:
        if len(current_run) >= 4:
            runs.append(current_run[:])
        current_run = []
if len(current_run) >= 4: runs.append(current_run)

print(f'Found {len(runs)} runs of 4+ printable ASCII constants:')
for run in sorted(runs, key=lambda r: -len(r))[:20]:
    s = ''.join(chr(v) for _,v in run)
    print(f'  len={len(run)} at idx[{run[0][0]}-{run[-1][0]}]: "{s[:60]}"')

# 4. Find specific constant values used in known Luau APIs
print('\n4. Constants that look like known values:')
special = {
    16: 'print/newline?', 32: 'space', 95: '_', 46: '.', 58: ':',
    0: 'nil/false', 1: 'true', 2: '2', 10: 'newline',
    65535: 'FFFF', 4294967295: 'UINT32_MAX', 2147483647: 'INT32_MAX',
    9007199254740992: '2^53 (MAX_SAFE_INT)', 4294967296: '2^32'
}
for i, v in enumerate(consts):
    if v in special:
        print(f'  const[{i}]={v} -> {special[v]}')
    if i < 100 and v > 1000000:
        # Check if large value is a known bit pattern
        try:
            f = struct.unpack('<d', struct.pack('<Q', v & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF))[0]
            if abs(f) != float('inf') and f == f:
                print(f'  const[{i}]={v} as float64={f:.8g}')
        except: pass

# 5. Identify CALL instructions - they appear before RETURNs and have predictable patterns
# In Lua: CALL R(A) B C -> calls function at R(A), B-1 args, C-1 returns
# After a CALL, the next instruction often uses the return values
print('\n5. Consecutive same-opcode pairs (potential CALL+RETURN or similar):')
pairs = Counter()
for i in range(numInstrs-1):
    if instrs[i][0] == instrs[i+1][0]:
        pairs[instrs[i][0]] += 1
for op, cnt in pairs.most_common(10):
    print(f'  op{op:02d} appears {cnt} times as consecutive pair')

# 6. Find jump targets by looking for instruction that appears at a 'regular interval'
# JMP instructions have a PC offset; the target offsets should form a pattern
print('\n6. Looking for JUMP instructions (fields might encode PC offsets):')
# In Luraph: JMP likely uses A as a signed offset (-128 to +127) or
# KX/UD as combined offset
# A common pattern: JMP appears frequently and has field=0 for some fields
for op in range(32):
    op_instrs = [(i, inst) for i, inst in enumerate(instrs) if inst[0]==op]
    if not op_instrs: continue
    # Check if A field has symmetric distribution (positive/negative offsets)
    a_vals = [AA(inst) for _,inst in op_instrs]
    a_neg = sum(1 for v in a_vals if v > 128)  # could be negative (signed)
    a_pos = sum(1 for v in a_vals if v <= 128)
    # Jumps might have balanced positive/negative counts
    ratio = min(a_neg, a_pos) / max(a_neg, a_pos, 1)
    if ratio > 0.3 and len(op_instrs) > 50:
        print(f'  op{op:02d}: A_pos={a_pos}, A_neg={a_neg} ratio={ratio:.2f} -> possible JUMP')

# 7. Find TEST-like instructions (appear just before JMP)
print('\n7. Instruction pairs analysis (what precedes each opcode):')
prev_op = Counter()
for i in range(1, numInstrs):
    prev_op[(instrs[i-1][0], instrs[i][0])] += 1
print('  Most common instruction pairs:')
for (op1,op2), cnt in prev_op.most_common(20):
    print(f'    op{op1:02d} -> op{op2:02d}: {cnt} times')

# 8. Look for constants that could be string table entries
print('\n8. Large constants that could be encoded floats/strings:')
large_const_hist = Counter()
for v in consts:
    bits = v.bit_length() if v > 0 else 0
    large_const_hist[bits//8] += 1
print('  Distribution by byte length:')
for size in sorted(large_const_hist):
    print(f'  {size} bytes: {large_const_hist[size]} constants')

# 9. Constants referenced by most common opcodes
print('\n9. Constants most referenced by op29 and op21 (via K field):')
for target_op in [29, 21, 31, 10, 3, 12]:
    op_instrs = [i for i in instrs if i[0]==target_op]
    k_refs = Counter(i[2] for i in op_instrs)  # K field (0-31)
    print(f'  op{target_op:02d} K field distribution: {dict(k_refs.most_common(5))}')
    # What constants do these K values point to?
    for k_val, cnt in k_refs.most_common(3):
        if k_val < len(consts):
            print(f'    K={k_val} ({cnt}x) -> const[{k_val}]={consts[k_val]}')

print('\nDone!')

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Decode the 62 sub-protos from decoded_payload.bin

Main proto layout (CONFIRMED):
  bytes 0-6:     5-field LEB128 header = [62, 5, 78, 11001, 10471]
  bytes 7-44010: 11001 instructions x 4 bytes each
  bytes 44011-65367: 10471 LEB128 constants
  bytes 65368-73403: 62 sub-protos (8036 bytes)

Goal: determine sub-proto format and decode all 62.
"""
import struct
from collections import Counter

with open('/data/decoded_payload.bin','rb') as f:
    data = bytearray(f.read())

SUBPROTO_START = 65368
FILE_END = len(data)  # 73404
NUM_SUBPROTOS = 62

print(f'=== SUB-PROTO DECODER ===')
print(f'Sub-proto section: bytes {SUBPROTO_START}-{FILE_END} ({FILE_END-SUBPROTO_START} bytes)')
print(f'Average sub-proto size: {(FILE_END-SUBPROTO_START)/NUM_SUBPROTOS:.1f} bytes')
print(f'\nFirst 40 bytes as hex:')
bytes40 = data[SUBPROTO_START:SUBPROTO_START+40]
print(' '.join(f'{b:02X}' for b in bytes40))

def read_leb128(data, pos):
    val, shift = 0, 0
    while pos < len(data):
        b = data[pos]; pos += 1
        val |= (b & 0x7F) << shift; shift += 7
        if not (b & 0x80): break
    return val, pos

# Try Format A: each sub-proto = [numInstrs(LEB128), instrs(4b each), numConsts(LEB128), consts(LEB128)]
# No sub-sub-protos for leaf closures
print(f'\n=== FORMAT A: [numInstrs, 4b instrs, numConsts, LEB128 consts] ===')
def try_format_a(data, start, num_protos):
    pos = start
    protos = []
    for i in range(num_protos):
        p_start = pos
        try:
            numInstrs, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
            if numInstrs > 10000 or numInstrs == 0:
                return None, f'Invalid numInstrs={numInstrs} at proto {i}'
            pos += numInstrs * 4  # skip instructions
            if pos >= len(data): return None, f'OOB after instrs in proto {i}'
            numConsts, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
            if numConsts > 100000: return None, f'Invalid numConsts={numConsts}'
            # Skip LEB128 constants
            for _ in range(numConsts):
                _, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
                if pos >= len(data): return None, f'OOB reading consts in proto {i}'
            protos.append((p_start, numInstrs, numConsts, pos-p_start))
        except Exception as e:
            return None, str(e)
    return protos, None

protos_a, err_a = try_format_a(data, SUBPROTO_START, NUM_SUBPROTOS)
if protos_a:
    sizes = [p[3] for p in protos_a]
    print(f'SUCCESS! End pos={SUBPROTO_START+sum(sizes)}, expected={FILE_END}')
    print(f'Size range: {min(sizes)}-{max(sizes)}, avg={sum(sizes)/len(sizes):.1f}')
    for i, p in enumerate(protos_a[:5]):
        print(f'  sub-proto[{i}]: instrs={p[1]}, consts={p[2]}, size={p[3]}')
else:
    print(f'FAILED: {err_a}')
    # Show first read attempt
    pos = SUBPROTO_START
    v, npos = read_leb128(data, pos)
    print(f'  First LEB128={v}, if numInstrs: would need {v*4} bytes for instructions')

# Try Format B: [numParams, maxStack, numInstrs, numConsts, 4b instrs, LEB128 consts]
print(f'\n=== FORMAT B: [numParams, maxStack, numInstrs, numConsts, 4b instrs, LEB128 consts] ===')
def try_format_b(data, start, num_protos):
    pos = start
    protos = []
    for i in range(num_protos):
        p_start = pos
        try:
            numParams, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
            maxStack, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
            numInstrs, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
            numConsts, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
            if numParams > 300 or maxStack > 300 or numInstrs > 10000:
                return None, f'Invalid fields at proto {i}: P={numParams} M={maxStack} I={numInstrs} C={numConsts}'
            pos += numInstrs * 4
            if pos >= len(data): return None, f'OOB after instrs in proto {i}'
            for _ in range(numConsts):
                _, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
                if pos >= len(data): return None, f'OOB reading consts in proto {i}'
            protos.append((p_start, numParams, maxStack, numInstrs, numConsts, pos-p_start))
        except Exception as e:
            return None, str(e)
    return protos, None

protos_b, err_b = try_format_b(data, SUBPROTO_START, NUM_SUBPROTOS)
if protos_b:
    sizes = [p[5] for p in protos_b]
    end_pos = SUBPROTO_START + sum(p[5] for p in protos_b)
    print(f'SUCCESS! End pos={end_pos}, expected={FILE_END}')
    print(f'Size range: {min(sizes)}-{max(sizes)}, avg={sum(sizes)/len(sizes):.1f}')
    for i, p in enumerate(protos_b[:5]):
        print(f'  sub-proto[{i}]: params={p[1]}, stack={p[2]}, instrs={p[3]}, consts={p[4]}, size={p[5]}')
else:
    print(f'FAILED: {err_b}')

# Try Format C: 5-field same as main [numSubSubProtos, numParams, maxStack, numInstrs, numConsts]
print(f'\n=== FORMAT C: 5-field like main proto ===')
def try_format_c(data, start, num_protos):
    pos = start
    protos = []
    for i in range(num_protos):
        p_start = pos
        try:
            numSubProtos2, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
            numParams, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
            maxStack, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
            numInstrs, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
            numConsts, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
            if numSubProtos2 > 100 or numParams > 300 or maxStack > 300 or numInstrs > 10000:
                return None, f'Invalid fields at proto {i}: SP={numSubProtos2} P={numParams} M={maxStack} I={numInstrs} C={numConsts}'
            pos += numInstrs * 4
            if pos >= len(data): return None, f'OOB after instrs in proto {i}'
            for _ in range(numConsts):
                _, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
                if pos >= len(data): return None, f'OOB reading consts in proto {i}'
            # Recursively handle sub-sub-protos
            sub_pos, e = try_format_c(data, pos, numSubProtos2)
            if e: return None, f'sub-proto error in proto {i}: {e}'
            if sub_pos: pos = sub_pos[-1][0] + sub_pos[-1][-1] if sub_pos else pos
            protos.append((p_start, numSubProtos2, numParams, maxStack, numInstrs, numConsts, pos-p_start))
        except Exception as e:
            return None, str(e)
    return protos, None

protos_c, err_c = try_format_c(data, SUBPROTO_START, NUM_SUBPROTOS)
if protos_c:
    sizes = [p[6] for p in protos_c]
    end_pos = sum(p[6] for p in protos_c) + SUBPROTO_START
    print(f'SUCCESS! End pos={end_pos}, expected={FILE_END}')
    for i, p in enumerate(protos_c[:5]):
        print(f'  sub-proto[{i}]: subprotos={p[1]}, params={p[2]}, stack={p[3]}, instrs={p[4]}, consts={p[5]}, size={p[6]}')
else:
    print(f'FAILED: {err_c}')

# Try Format D: 2-byte instructions instead of 4
print(f'\n=== FORMAT D: 4-field + 2-byte instructions ===')
def try_format_d(data, start, num_protos, instr_size=2):
    pos = start
    protos = []
    for i in range(num_protos):
        p_start = pos
        try:
            numParams, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
            maxStack, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
            numInstrs, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
            numConsts, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
            if numParams > 300 or maxStack > 300 or numInstrs > 10000:
                return None, f'Invalid at proto {i}: P={numParams} M={maxStack} I={numInstrs} C={numConsts}'
            pos += numInstrs * instr_size
            if pos >= len(data): return None, f'OOB after instrs in proto {i}'
            for _ in range(numConsts):
                _, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
                if pos >= len(data): return None, f'OOB reading consts in proto {i}'
            protos.append((p_start, numParams, maxStack, numInstrs, numConsts, pos-p_start))
        except Exception as e:
            return None, str(e)
    return protos, None

protos_d, err_d = try_format_d(data, SUBPROTO_START, NUM_SUBPROTOS, 2)
if protos_d:
    sizes = [p[5] for p in protos_d]
    end_pos = SUBPROTO_START + sum(p[5] for p in protos_d)
    print(f'SUCCESS! End pos={end_pos}, expected={FILE_END}')

else:
    print(f'FAILED: {err_d}')

# Try Format E: SIZE prefix + content
print(f'\n=== FORMAT E: SIZE(LEB128) prefix, then content bytes ===')
def try_format_e(data, start, num_protos):

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Deep sub-proto analysis with many format attempts"""
import struct
from collections import Counter

with open('/data/decoded_payload.bin','rb') as f:

FILE_END = 73404

def read_leb128(data, pos):
    val, shift = 0, 0
    while pos < len(data):
        b = data[pos]; pos += 1
        val |= (b & 0x7F) << shift; shift += 7
        if not (b & 0x80): break
    return val, pos

def leb128_size(val):
    if val == 0: return 1
    size = 0
    while val > 0: val >>= 7; size += 1
    return size

# Show first 100 bytes hex

    p1_numInstrs, pos1 = read_leb128(data, pos1)
    p1_numConsts, pos1 = read_leb128(data, pos1)
    print(f'  proto[1] Format B fields: params={p1_numParams}, stack={p1_maxStack}, instrs={p1_numInstrs}, consts={p1_numConsts}')
    p1_instr_end = pos1 + p1_numInstrs * 4
    p1_expected_total = pos1 + p1_numInstrs*4 + p1_numConsts*2
    print(f'  proto[1] instrs would take {p1_numInstrs*4} bytes, ending at {p1_instr_end}')
    print(f'  proto[1] rough size estimate: {p1_expected_total - proto1_start} bytes')

# Now try 2-byte instruction format recursively
print('\n--- Format: 5-field + 2-byte instrs (recursive) ---')
def parse_proto_2b(data, pos, depth=0, max_depth=5):
    if pos >= FILE_END or depth > max_depth:
        return None, pos
    p_start = pos
    try:
        f1, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
        f2, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
        f3, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
        f4, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
        f5, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
        # Try different field orderings
        # Order 1: [numSubProtos, numParams, maxStack, numInstrs, numConsts]
        numSP, numP, numS, numI, numC = f1, f2, f3, f4, f5
        if numI > 10000 or numC > 100000 or numSP > 500:
            return None, p_start
        instr_bytes = numI * 2  # 2-byte instructions
        if pos + instr_bytes > FILE_END:
            return None, p_start
        pos += instr_bytes
        for _ in range(numC):
            if pos >= FILE_END: return None, p_start
            _, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
        # Recursively parse numSP sub-protos
        sub_protos = []
        for _ in range(numSP):
            sp, pos = parse_proto_2b(data, pos, depth+1)
            if sp is None: return None, p_start
            sub_protos.append(sp)
        return {'fields': (f1,f2,f3,f4,f5), 'sub_protos': sub_protos, 'size': pos-p_start}, pos
    except:
        return None, p_start

# Parse single top-level sub-proto[0]
result, end_pos = parse_proto_2b(data, SP_START)
if result:
    print(f'  Parsed proto[0]! Size={result["size"]} bytes, end={SP_START+result["size"]}')
    print(f'  Fields: {result["fields"]}')
    print(f'  Sub-protos: {len(result["sub_protos"])}')
    print(f'  Remaining after: {FILE_END - end_pos} bytes')
else:
    print('  Failed to parse with 2-byte instrs')

# Try treating entire section as FLAT instruction buffer (4-byte)
print('\n--- Flat 4-byte instruction buffer analysis ---')
num_flat_instrs = TOTAL_SP_BYTES // 4
print(f'  Total flat instructions: {num_flat_instrs} ({TOTAL_SP_BYTES} / 4)')
op_counts = Counter()
for i in range(num_flat_instrs):
    bp = SP_START + i*4
    A,B,C,D = data[bp], data[bp+1], data[bp+2], data[bp+3]
    op = B>>3
    op_counts[op] += 1
print(f'  Opcode distribution (from flat decode):')
for op, cnt in sorted(op_counts.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1]):
    print(f'    op{op:02d}: {cnt} ({100*cnt/num_flat_instrs:.1f}%)')

# Compare with MAIN proto opcode distribution
with open('/data/full_disasm.json') as f:
    import json
    main = json.load(f)
main_instrs = main['instrs']
main_ops = Counter(i[0] for i in main_instrs)
print(f'\n  Opcode comparison (main vs flat sub-proto):')
print(f'  {"OP":>5} {"MAIN%":>8} {"SUBPROTO%":>10}')
for op in range(32):
    mp = 100*main_ops.get(op,0)/len(main_instrs)
    sp = 100*op_counts.get(op,0)/num_flat_instrs
    if mp > 1 or sp > 1:
        print(f'  op{op:02d}: {mp:7.1f}% {sp:9.1f}%')

# Try to find function boundaries by looking for RETURN-like sequences
print('\n--- Looking for function boundaries in flat decode ---')
# Common patterns: opcodes with special terminal meaning
# In Lua: RETURN usually at end of functions
# Try to find repeating opcodes that could be proto separators
print('  First 50 flat instructions:')
for i in range(50):
    bp = SP_START + i*4
    A,B,C,D = data[bp], data[bp+1], data[bp+2], data[bp+3]
    op, S = B>>3, B&7
    K, x = C>>3, C&7
    U, d = D>>3, D&7
    print(f'  [{i:3d}] op{op:02d} S={S} K={K} x={x} U={U} d={d} A={A}')

# Try encoding the sub-proto section as raw LEB128 stream
print('\n--- Reading sub-proto section as LEB128 stream ---')
pos = SP_START
lebs = []
while pos < min(SP_START+200, FILE_END):
    v, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
    lebs.append(v)
print(f'  First {len(lebs)} LEB128 values: {lebs[:40]}')
print(f'  Values < 128: {sum(1 for v in lebs if v < 128)}/{len(lebs)}')
print(f'  Values < 10471 (const ref): {sum(1 for v in lebs if v < 10471)}/{len(lebs)}')

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Full sub-proto decoder: proto[0] uses Format B, proto[1-61] use unknown format.
Goal: determine proto[1-61] format and disassemble all instructions."""
import struct, json
from collections import Counter

with open('/data/decoded_payload.bin','rb') as f:
    data = bytearray(f.read())

SP_START = 65368
FILE_END = 73404
NUM_SUBPROTOS = 62

def read_leb128(data, pos):
    val, shift = 0, 0
    while pos < len(data):
        b = data[pos]; pos += 1
        val |= (b & 0x7F) << shift; shift += 7
        if not (b & 0x80): break
    return val, pos

# Step 1: Parse proto[0] with Format B
pos = SP_START
numParams0, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
numStack0, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
numInstrs0, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
numConsts0, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)

print(f'proto[0]: params={numParams0}, stack={numStack0}, instrs={numInstrs0}, consts={numConsts0}')

# Read instructions (4-byte each)
instrs0 = []
for i in range(numInstrs0):
    bp = pos + i*4
    A,B,C,D = data[bp],data[bp+1],data[bp+2],data[bp+3]
    instrs0.append((B>>3, B&7, C>>3, C&7, D>>3, D&7, A))
pos += numInstrs0 * 4

# Read constants (LEB128)
consts0 = []
for i in range(numConsts0):
    v, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
    consts0.append(v)

proto0_end = pos
print(f'proto[0] ends at byte {proto0_end}, size={proto0_end-SP_START}')
print(f'Remaining for proto[1-61]: {FILE_END-proto0_end} bytes for {NUM_SUBPROTOS-1} protos')

# Print proto[0] instructions
print('\nproto[0] instructions (all 47):')
for i, (op,S,K,x,U,d,A) in enumerate(instrs0):
    const_ref = consts0[K] if K < len(consts0) else '?'
    print(f'  [{i:3d}] op{op:02d} S={S} K={K}(={const_ref}) x={x} U={U} d={d} A={A}')

print(f'\nproto[0] first 20 consts: {consts0[:20]}')
print(f'proto[0] const range: {min(consts0)}-{max(consts0)}')

# Step 2: Try different formats for proto[1-61]
remaining = FILE_END - proto0_end  # 1553
num_remaining = NUM_SUBPROTOS - 1  # 61

print(f'\n=== Trying formats for proto[1-61] ({remaining} bytes for {num_remaining} protos) ===')

def try_format_remaining(start, num, instr_size, header_fields, with_consts=False):
    """Try parsing num protos from start.
    header_fields: number of LEB128 fields before instructions.
    The LAST header field is always numInstrs.
    instr_size: bytes per instruction.
    Returns: list of (numInstrs, size) or None.
    """
    pos = start
    protos = []
    for i in range(num):
        p_start = pos
        fields = []
        try:
            for _ in range(header_fields):
                v, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
                fields.append(v)
            numInstrs = fields[-1]  # last field = numInstrs
            if numInstrs > 10000:
                return None, f'numInstrs={numInstrs} too large at proto[{i+1}]'
            pos += numInstrs * instr_size
            if pos > FILE_END:
                return None, f'OOB at proto[{i+1}]'
            if with_consts:
                numConsts, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
                if numConsts > 10000: return None, f'numConsts={numConsts} too large'
                for _ in range(numConsts):
                    _, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
                    if pos > FILE_END: return None, 'OOB reading consts'
            protos.append((fields, numInstrs, pos-p_start))
        except Exception as e:
            return None, str(e)
    total = pos - start
    if abs(total - remaining) > 2:
        return None, f'Total {total} != expected {remaining}'
    return protos, None

best_formats = []
for instr_size in [1, 2, 4]:
    for n_header in [1, 2, 3]:
        for with_consts in [False, True]:
            protos, err = try_format_remaining(proto0_end, num_remaining, instr_size, n_header, with_consts)
            if protos:
                desc = f'[{n_header} header fields, {instr_size}b instrs{" + consts" if with_consts else ""}]'
                sizes = [p[2] for p in protos]
                ninstrs = [p[1] for p in protos]
                print(f'  SUCCESS: {desc}')
                print(f'    Size range: {min(sizes)}-{max(sizes)}, avg={sum(sizes)/len(sizes):.1f}')
                print(f'    numInstrs range: {min(ninstrs)}-{max(ninstrs)}, avg={sum(ninstrs)/len(ninstrs):.1f}')
                print(f'    First 5 protos fields: {[p[0] for p in protos[:5]]}')
                best_formats.append((instr_size, n_header, with_consts, protos))

if not best_formats:
    print('  No matching format found! Trying looser constraints...')
    # Try without exact end constraint
    for instr_size in [1, 2, 4]:
        for n_header in [1, 2, 3]:
            pos = proto0_end
            partial_ok = 0
            for i in range(num_remaining):
                try:
                    fields = []
                    for _ in range(n_header):
                        v, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
                        fields.append(v)
                    numInstrs = fields[-1]
                    if numInstrs > 500:
                        break
                    pos += numInstrs * instr_size
                    if pos > FILE_END: break
                    partial_ok += 1
                except: break
            if partial_ok > 5:
                print(f'  Partial success: {n_header} header, {instr_size}b instrs: parsed {partial_ok}/{num_remaining} protos')

# Step 3: If we found a good format, decode all instructions
if best_formats:
    instr_size, n_header, with_consts, protos_data = best_formats[0]
    print(f'\n=== Full decode with best format: {n_header} header fields, {instr_size}b instrs ===')
    
    pos = proto0_end
    all_protos = []
    for i in range(num_remaining):
        p_start = pos
        fields = []
        for _ in range(n_header):
            v, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
            fields.append(v)
        numInstrs = fields[-1]
        
        instrs = []
        for j in range(numInstrs):
            bp = pos + j * instr_size
            if instr_size == 1:
                b = data[bp]
                op, operand = b>>3, b&7
                instrs.append((op, operand))
            elif instr_size == 2:
                b0, b1 = data[bp], data[bp+1]
                op = b0>>3
                instrs.append((op, b0&7, b1))
            elif instr_size == 4:
                A,B,C,D = data[bp],data[bp+1],data[bp+2],data[bp+3]
                instrs.append((B>>3, B&7, C>>3, C&7, D>>3, D&7, A))
        pos += numInstrs * instr_size
        
        consts_local = []
        if with_consts:
            numConsts, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
            for _ in range(numConsts):
                v, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
                consts_local.append(v)
        
        all_protos.append({'fields': fields, 'instrs': instrs, 'consts': consts_local})
    
    # Print first 5 protos
    for i, p in enumerate(all_protos[:5]):
        print(f'\nproto[{i+1}]: fields={p["fields"]}, instrs={len(p["instrs"])}, consts={len(p["consts"])}')
        for j, instr in enumerate(p['instrs'][:20]):
            print(f'  [{j}] {instr}')
    
    # Opcode analysis
    op_counts = Counter()
    for p in all_protos:
        for instr in p['instrs']:
            op_counts[instr[0]] += 1
    
    total_instrs = sum(op_counts.values())
    print(f'\nOpcode distribution ({total_instrs} total instructions):')
    for op, cnt in sorted(op_counts.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1]):
        print(f'  op{op:02d}: {cnt} ({100*cnt/total_instrs:.1f}%)')
    
    # Save results
    result = {
        'proto0': {
            'params': numParams0,
            'stack': numStack0,
            'instrs': [(op,S,K,x,U,d,A) for op,S,K,x,U,d,A in instrs0],
            'consts': consts0[:200]  # first 200
        },
        'subprotos': [{
            'fields': p['fields'],
            'instrs': p['instrs'][:100],  # first 100
            'consts': p['consts'][:50]
        } for p in all_protos]
    }
    with open('/data/subproto_decoded.json','w') as f:
        json.dump(result, f)
    print('\nSaved to /data/subproto_decoded.json')

print('\nDone.')

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Full program decode: verify 2-byte instruction format for proto[1-61]"""
import json, struct
from collections import Counter

with open('/data/decoded_payload.bin','rb') as f:
    data = bytearray(f.read())

FILE_END = 73404
SP_START = 65368

def read_leb128(data, pos):
    val, shift = 0, 0
    start = pos
    while pos < len(data):
        b = data[pos]; pos += 1
        val |= (b & 0x7F) << shift; shift += 7
        if not (b & 0x80): break
    return val, pos

# Step 1: re-parse proto[0] with Format B to get to proto[1] start
pos = SP_START
numP0, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)  # 101
numS0, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)  # 68
numI0, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)  # 47
numC0, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)  # 3075

# Skip instructions
instrs0_start = pos
pos += numI0 * 4  # 47 * 4 = 188 bytes

# Read constants
consts0 = []
for _ in range(numC0):
    v, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
    consts0.append(v)

proto1_start = pos
print(f'proto[1] starts at byte {proto1_start}')
print(f'Remaining: {FILE_END - proto1_start} bytes')

# Dump 100 bytes at proto[1] start
print(f'\nBytes at proto[1] ({proto1_start}):')  
for i in range(0, 128, 16):
    bp = proto1_start + i
    if bp >= FILE_END: break
    row = data[bp:min(bp+16, FILE_END)]
    hex_str = ' '.join(f'{b:02X}' for b in row)
    asc_str = ''.join(chr(b) if 32<=b<127 else '.' for b in row)
    print(f'  {bp}: {hex_str:<48} |{asc_str}|')

# Step 2: Try ALL formats for proto[1] onwards
# key insight: numInstrs(1b) + 2b instructions is confirmed for proto[1]
# but we don't know the HEADER format: is there numParams? numStack? etc.

print('\n=== TRACING FORMAT OPTIONS ===')

# Parse proto[1] with [1 header byte = numInstrs, then 2b instrs]
# and check what byte comes AFTER the instructions
p1_numInstrs = 116
p1_instr_end = proto1_start + 1 + p1_numInstrs * 2  # 1 header + 232 instr bytes = 233 bytes
print(f'\nproto[1] instruction block end: byte {p1_instr_end}')
print(f'Bytes at that position ({p1_instr_end}):')
for i in range(0, 48, 16):
    bp = p1_instr_end + i
    if bp >= FILE_END: break
    row = data[bp:min(bp+16, FILE_END)]
    hex_str = ' '.join(f'{b:02X}' for b in row)
    print(f'  {bp}: {hex_str}')

# Try different counts of additional header bytes for proto[1]
for extra_header in [0, 1, 2, 3]:
    # proto[1] = 1(numInstrs) + extra_header(?) + numInstrs*2(instrs) + maybe consts
    p1_data_start = proto1_start + 1 + extra_header  # skip numInstrs + extra headers
    p1_data_end = p1_data_start + p1_numInstrs * 2
    if p1_data_end > FILE_END: continue
    
    # What's after proto[1] instructions?
    byte_after = p1_data_end
    next_byte = data[byte_after] if byte_after < FILE_END else None
    print(f'  extra_header={extra_header}: proto[1] ends at {p1_data_end}, next byte={next_byte:02X}' if next_byte is not None else f'  extra_header={extra_header}: OOB')

# Step 3: Brute force scan from proto1_start to find consistent proto boundaries
print('\n=== BRUTE FORCE BOUNDARY SCAN ===')
# Try to find: how many 2-byte instructions follow header byte 0x74=116?
# Then look at what's AFTER to determine remaining proto formats

candidate_positions = []
for instr_count in [116, 24, 68, 47, 101]:
    for extra_hdr in [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]:
        end = proto1_start + 1 + extra_hdr + instr_count * 2
        if end < FILE_END:
            next_b = data[end]
            end2 = end
            # Try reading a LEB128 from end (potential numInstrs for next proto or numConsts)
            v2, end2 = read_leb128(data, end)
            candidate_positions.append((instr_count, extra_hdr, end, next_b, v2))
            
print('  (numInstrs, extra_hdr, end_pos, next_byte, next_leb128):')
for c in candidate_positions[:20]:
    print(f'  numI={c[0]:3d} hdr={c[1]} end={c[2]} next_b={c[3]:02X}({c[3]:3d}) next_leb128={c[4]}')

# Step 4: Scan from proto1_start for self-consistent proto sequence
# Try format: each proto = [numInstrs(1b), numInstrs×2b instrs]
# and check if 61 such protos fit in exactly FILE_END-proto1_start bytes
print('\n=== GREEDY PROTO BOUNDARY DETECTION ===')

# Method 1: [numInstrs(1b), 2b instrs], NO consts
pos = proto1_start
sizes1 = []
valid = True
for i in range(61):
    if pos >= FILE_END:
        valid = False; break
    numI = data[pos]; pos += 1
    if numI * 2 > FILE_END - pos:
        valid = False; break
    pos += numI * 2
    sizes1.append(numI)
print(f'Method 1 [numInstrs+2b_instrs]: valid={valid}, end={pos}, target={FILE_END}')
if sizes1:
    print(f'  numInstrs stats: min={min(sizes1)}, max={max(sizes1)}, avg={sum(sizes1)/len(sizes1):.1f}')
    print(f'  First 10 numInstrs: {sizes1[:10]}')

# Method 2: [numInstrs(2b LEB128), numInstrs×2b instrs]
pos = proto1_start
sizes2 = []
valid2 = True
for i in range(61):
    if pos >= FILE_END:
        valid2 = False; break
    numI, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
    if numI * 2 > FILE_END - pos or numI > 10000:
        valid2 = False; break
    pos += numI * 2
    sizes2.append(numI)
print(f'Method 2 [LEB128_numInstrs+2b_instrs]: valid={valid2}, end={pos}, target={FILE_END}')
if sizes2:
    print(f'  numInstrs: {sizes2[:10]}')

# Method 3: [numInstrs(1b), 2b instrs, numConsts(1b), 1b consts]
pos = proto1_start
sizes3 = []
valid3 = True
for i in range(61):
    if pos >= FILE_END: valid3=False; break
    numI = data[pos]; pos += 1
    if pos + numI*2 > FILE_END: valid3=False; break
    pos += numI * 2  
    if pos >= FILE_END: valid3=False; break
    numC = data[pos]; pos += 1
    if pos + numC > FILE_END: valid3=False; break
    pos += numC
    sizes3.append((numI, numC))
print(f'Method 3 [numI+2b_instrs+numC+1b_consts]: valid={valid3}, end={pos}, target={FILE_END}')
if sizes3:
    print(f'  (numI, numC) first 10: {sizes3[:10]}')

# Method 4: flat 2-byte instruction stream (no headers)
# 61 protos divides the flat buffer somehow
flat_2b_count = (FILE_END - proto1_start) // 2
print(f'\nFlat 2b count: {flat_2b_count} instructions for {FILE_END-proto1_start} bytes')
print(f'Per proto: {flat_2b_count/61:.1f} instructions')

# Method 5: scan for 'size header' format
# each proto starts with SIZE(1b) = total bytes INCLUDING this header byte  
pos = proto1_start
sizes5 = []
valid5 = True
for i in range(61):
    if pos >= FILE_END: valid5=False; break
    sz = data[pos]; pos_after = pos + sz
    if pos_after > FILE_END: valid5=False; break
    sizes5.append(sz)
    pos = pos_after
print(f'Method 5 [SIZE_prefix]: valid={valid5}, end={pos}, target={FILE_END}')
if sizes5 and valid5:
    print(f'  Sizes: {sizes5}')

# Method 6: each proto has 2b header = [numParams(1b), numInstrs(1b)], then 2b instrs
pos = proto1_start  
sizes6 = []
valid6 = True
for i in range(61):
    if pos+1 >= FILE_END: valid6=False; break
    numP = data[pos]; numI = data[pos+1]; pos += 2
    if pos + numI*2 > FILE_END: valid6=False; break
    pos += numI * 2
    sizes6.append((numP, numI))
print(f'Method 6 [numP+numI+2b_instrs]: valid={valid6}, end={pos}, target={FILE_END}')
if sizes6:
    print(f'  First 10: {sizes6[:10]}')

# Step 5: What do the bytes around the boundary look like?
print('\n=== KEY BYTE RANGES ===')
for label, start, length in [
    ('proto1_header+instrs', proto1_start, 240),
    ('after_proto1_instrs', proto1_start+233, 100),
    ('last_100_bytes', FILE_END-100, 100),
]:
    print(f'\n{label} (bytes {start}-{start+length-1}):')
    for i in range(0, length, 16):
        bp = start + i
        if bp >= FILE_END: break
        row = data[bp:min(bp+16, FILE_END)]
        hex_str = ' '.join(f'{b:02X}' for b in row)
        asc_str = ''.join(chr(b) if 32<=b<127 else '.' for b in row)
        print(f'  {bp}: {hex_str:<48} |{asc_str}|')

print('\nDone.')

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Verify: proto[1]=233 bytes (1hdr+116*2b), proto[2-61]=22 bytes each (11*2b flat, NO headers)
Total: 233 + 60*22 = 1553 bytes EXACTLY"""
import json
from collections import Counter

with open('/data/decoded_payload.bin','rb') as f:
    data = bytearray(f.read())

FILE_END = 73404
SP_START = 65368

def read_leb128(data, pos):
    val, shift = 0, 0
    while pos < len(data):
        b = data[pos]; pos += 1
        val |= (b & 0x7F) << shift; shift += 7
        if not (b & 0x80): break
    return val, pos

# Parse proto[0]
pos = SP_START
numP0, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
numS0, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
numI0, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
numC0, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
pos += numI0 * 4
consts0 = []
for _ in range(numC0):
    v, pos = read_leb128(data, pos)
    consts0.append(v)

proto1_start = pos  # 71851
print(f'proto[1] starts at byte {proto1_start}')
print(f'proto[0] consts[0:50]: {consts0[:50]}')

# Step 1: Proto[1] = 1 byte header + 116*2b instructions
p1_numInstrs = data[proto1_start]  # 0x74 = 116
p1_instr_start = proto1_start + 1
p1_instr_end = p1_instr_start + p1_numInstrs * 2  # 71852 + 232 = 72084

print(f'\nproto[1]: numInstrs={p1_numInstrs}, instr_start={p1_instr_start}, instr_end={p1_instr_end}')

# Step 2: proto[2-61] = flat 22-byte blocks (11 2-byte instructions each)
proto2_start = p1_instr_end  # 72084
FIXED_SIZE = 22  # 11 * 2
NUM_REMAINING = 60  # proto[2-61]

# Verify total
total_subproto = (1 + p1_numInstrs*2) + NUM_REMAINING * FIXED_SIZE
expected = FILE_END - proto1_start  # 1553
print(f'\nVerification: {1+p1_numInstrs*2} + {NUM_REMAINING}*{FIXED_SIZE} = {total_subproto} (expected {expected})')
print(f'Match: {total_subproto == expected}')

# Check last proto ends exactly at FILE_END
last_proto_start = proto2_start + (NUM_REMAINING - 1) * FIXED_SIZE
last_proto_end = last_proto_start + FIXED_SIZE
print(f'Last proto[61]: {last_proto_start} - {last_proto_end-1} (FILE_END = {FILE_END})')
print(f'Last 4 bytes: {" ".join(f"{data[i]:02X}" for i in range(FILE_END-4, FILE_END))}')

# Step 3: Decode ALL instructions
def decode_2b(byte0, byte1):
    op = byte0 >> 3
    field = byte0 & 7
    arg = byte1
    return (op, field, arg)

def decode_4b(A, B, C, D):
    return {'op': B>>3, 'S': B&7, 'K': C>>3, 'x': C&7, 'U': D>>3, 'd': D&7, 'A': A}

# Decode proto[0] instructions
instrs0 = []
for i in range(numI0):
    bp = SP_START + 4 + i*4  # skip 4-field header (variable length!)
# Actually header is LEB128 → need to recalculate
pos_i0 = SP_START
for _ in range(4): _, pos_i0 = read_leb128(data, pos_i0)
for i in range(numI0):
    bp = pos_i0 + i*4
    instrs0.append(decode_4b(data[bp], data[bp+1], data[bp+2], data[bp+3]))

# Decode proto[1] instructions  
instrs1 = []
for i in range(p1_numInstrs):
    bp = p1_instr_start + i*2
    instrs1.append(decode_2b(data[bp], data[bp+1]))

# Decode proto[2-61] instructions
all_subprotos = []  # list of list of instrs
for k in range(NUM_REMAINING):
    start = proto2_start + k * FIXED_SIZE
    instrs_k = []
    for i in range(11):
        bp = start + i*2
        instrs_k.append(decode_2b(data[bp], data[bp+1]))
    all_subprotos.append(instrs_k)

# Step 4: Print proto[1] instructions with const annotations
print(f'\n=== PROTO[1] INSTRUCTIONS (116 2-byte instrs) ===')
for i, (op, field, arg) in enumerate(instrs1):
    const_val = consts0[arg] if arg < len(consts0) else '?'
    print(f'  [{i:3d}] op{op:02d} f={field} arg={arg:3d} (const={const_val})')

# Step 5: Print first 10 sub-proto handlers
print(f'\n=== PROTO[2-61] HANDLERS (11 instructions each) ===')
for k in range(10):
    print(f'\nproto[{k+2}]:')
    for i, (op, field, arg) in enumerate(all_subprotos[k]):
        const_val = consts0[arg] if arg < len(consts0) else '?'
        print(f'  [{i}] op{op:02d} f={field} arg={arg:3d} (const={const_val})')

# Step 6: Analyze OPCODE DISTRIBUTION across all protos
op_counts = Counter()
for op,f,arg in instrs1:
    op_counts[op] += 1
for handler in all_subprotos:
    for op,f,arg in handler:
        op_counts[op] += 1

total_i = sum(op_counts.values())
print(f'\n=== OPCODE DISTRIBUTION (all 776 instructions) ===')
for op, cnt in sorted(op_counts.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1]):
    print(f'  op{op:02d}: {cnt:4d} ({100*cnt/total_i:5.1f}%)')

# Step 7: Find common instruction patterns
print(f'\n=== COMMON INSTRUCTION PATTERNS ===')
pattern_counter = Counter()
for handler in all_subprotos:
    for instr in handler:
        pattern_counter[instr] += 1
for instr, cnt in pattern_counter.most_common(20):
    const_val = consts0[instr[2]] if instr[2] < len(consts0) else '?'
    print(f'  {instr} (const[{instr[2]}]={const_val}): {cnt}/{len(all_subprotos)} protos')

# Step 8: Analyze which positions are INVARIANT vs VARIANT
print(f'\n=== POSITION ANALYSIS (invariant positions in proto[2-61]) ===')
for pos_in in range(11):
    instrs_at_pos = [all_subprotos[k][pos_in] for k in range(NUM_REMAINING)]
    unique_ops = set(i[0] for i in instrs_at_pos)
    unique_full = set(instrs_at_pos)
    if len(unique_full) == 1:
        print(f'  pos[{pos_in}]: INVARIANT = {unique_full.pop()}')
    elif len(unique_ops) == 1:
        # Same opcode, different args
        op = list(unique_ops)[0]
        args = [i[2] for i in instrs_at_pos]
        print(f'  pos[{pos_in}]: op{op:02d} FIXED (args vary: {min(args)}-{max(args)}, unique={len(set(args))})')
    else:
        print(f'  pos[{pos_in}]: VARIANT (ops: {sorted(unique_ops)[:5]}, {len(unique_full)} unique instructions)')

# Step 9: Save complete decode
result = {
    'proto0': {
        'format': '4-byte instructions',
        'numParams': numP0, 'maxStack': numS0, 'numInstrs': numI0, 'numConsts': numC0,
        'consts': consts0,
        'instrs': [{'op':x['op'],'S':x['S'],'K':x['K'],'U':x['U'],'A':x['A']} for x in instrs0]
    },
    'proto1': {

    }

print('Most common args (top 20):')

    print(f'  arg={arg:3d} (const={const_val}): {cnt} times')

# Step 11: Look for semantic patterns
print('\n=== OPCODE SEMANTIC HINTS ===')
# In proto[1]: what's the FIRST instruction opcode for context?

# Most common opcode in proto[2-61] FIRST position
first_ops = Counter(all_subprotos[k][0][0] for k in range(NUM_REMAINING))

# Most common opcode in proto[2-61] LAST position
last_ops = Counter(all_subprotos[k][-1][0] for k in range(NUM_REMAINING))
print(f'Last instruction op in handlers: {last_ops.most_common(10)}')

import sys
def patch(p, reps):

  hooks?: PyHook[];

"""  /** Python name of the Lua parameter / upvalue `lua` visible at the top of `f`'s body (last duplicate parameter wins) */
  visibleName(f: A.FunctionExpr, pyParams: string[], lua: string): string | null {

    if (i >= 0) return pyParams[i];
    const fl = f.loc;

cd /data/prism/packages/tools && cat > src/tools/lift.ts <<'EOF'
// One-click VM lifting — universal: works on any interpreter findVmShape recognises, nothing obfuscator-specific.
//   vm_boot_dump  the decoded chunk without reversing its format: the loader, ported to Python, runs on its own
//                 payload and is stopped at the VM closure factory, which dumps proto / upvalues / env / helper tables
//   vm_lift       boot dump → helper library + pure wrapper slots → vmSpecialize on every proto → lifted Lua script
import { z } from 'zod';
import { existsSync, readFileSync, statSync, rmSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join, delimiter } from 'node:path';
import { defineTool } from '../types.js';
import type { ToolContext } from '../types.js';
import { SRC, OUT, getSource, table } from '../source.js';
import { vmBootProgram, vmFactoryInfo, helperWrapperRules, vmSpecialize, findVmShape, parse, clean } from '@prism/core';
import { runNative } from '../native.js';
import { saveDerived } from './deob.js';

/** python3 on the PRISM host: explicit path, $PRISM_PYTHON, then PATH */
export function findPython(explicit?: string): string | null {
  for (const c of [explicit, process.env.PRISM_PYTHON]) if (c && existsSync(c)) return c;
  const names = process.platform === 'win32' ? ['python.exe', 'python3.exe', 'py.exe'] : ['python3', 'python'];
  const dirs = (process.env.PATH ?? '').split(delimiter).filter(Boolean);
  for (const n of names) for (const d of dirs) if (existsSync(join(d, n))) return join(d, n);
  return null;
}

const baseName = (ctx: ToolContext, scriptId: string | undefined): string =>
  ((scriptId && ctx.ws.getMeta(scriptId)?.name) || scriptId || 'inline').replace(/\.(lua|luau|txt)$/i, '');

const NO_VM = 'no VM interpreter recognised (a dispatch loop over decoded instructions + the closure factory that creates VM closures), not even after cleaning — vm_detect / vm_anatomy show what is there';

/** the script the VM tools need: the given one when its interpreter is recognisable, else its cleaned copy */
function vmSource(ctx: ToolContext, src: string, base: string, scriptId: string | undefined): { ok: boolean; src: string; scriptId?: string; line?: string } {
  if (findVmShape(parse(src).chunk).shape) return { ok: true, src, scriptId };
  const c = clean(src, { rename: 'obfuscated' });
  if (!findVmShape(parse(c.code).chunk).shape) return { ok: false, src, scriptId };
  const sv = saveDerived(ctx, base + '.clean.lua', c.code, scriptId, 'deobfuscate (vm_lift)');
  return { ok: true, src: c.code, scriptId: sv.id, line: 'cleaned first → ' + sv.line };
}

const BOOT_IN = {
  python: z.string().optional().describe('python executable (default: $PRISM_PYTHON, then python3 / python on PATH)'),
  timeout_s: z.number().int().min(5).max(3600).optional().describe('run-time limit of the boot program in seconds (default 300)'),
  extra: z.array(z.string()).optional().describe('extra Lua names visible in the closure factory to put in the dump'),
  save_dump_as: z.string().optional().describe('dump output name (default <script>.vmdump.json)'),
};

interface BootRun { ok: boolean; lines: string[]; dump?: unknown; dumpName?: string; program?: string; helper?: { name: string; path: string } }

async function bootDump(ctx: ToolContext, src: string, base: string, a: { python?: string; timeout_s?: number; extra?: string[]; save_dump_as?: string; run?: boolean }): Promise<BootRun> {
  const dumpName = a.save_dump_as ?? base + '.vmdump.json';
  const dumpRel = ctx.ws.saveOutput(dumpName, '');
  const dumpAbs = ctx.ws.abs(dumpRel);
  rmSync(dumpAbs, { force: true });
  const embed = a.run !== false;
  const boot = vmBootProgram(src, { dumpPath: embed ? dumpAbs : undefined, extra: a.extra });
  const lines = [...boot.notes.map(n => '# ' + n), ...boot.warnings.map(w => '# warning: ' + w)];
  if (!boot.ok) return { ok: false, lines: [...lines, 'no VM closure factory to hook'] };
  const program = ctx.ws.saveOutput(base + '.boot.py', boot.program);
  const helper = boot.info?.helper;
  lines.push(`boot program: ${program} (${boot.program.length} chars; dump keys: ${boot.keys.join(', ')})`);
  if (!embed) return { ok: false, lines: [...lines, `run it: python3 ${base}.boot.py ${dumpName}  — then vm_lift {dump:"<that file>"} (or workspace_save_output it and pass the output name)`], program, helper };
  const py = findPython(a.python);
  if (!py) return { ok: false, lines: [...lines, `python3 not found on the PRISM host (set PRISM_PYTHON, or run: python3 "${ctx.ws.abs(program)}" — it writes ${dumpRel}; then vm_lift {dump:"${dumpName}"})`], program, helper };
  const r = await runNative(py, [ctx.ws.abs(program)], { timeoutMs: (a.timeout_s ?? 300) * 1000, maxBytes: 8 << 20 });
  const size = existsSync(dumpAbs) ? statSync(dumpAbs).size : 0;
  if (!size) {
    rmSync(dumpAbs, { force: true });
    const tail = String(r.stderr || r.stdout || '').trim().split('\n').slice(-25).join('\n');
    return { ok: false, lines: [...lines, `the boot program did not reach the closure factory (exit ${r.code}${r.timedOut ? ', timed out' : ''}, ${r.ms} ms):`, tail], program, helper };
  }
  lines.push(`dump: ${dumpRel} (${size} bytes; python ${r.ms} ms)`);
  return { ok: true, lines, dump: JSON.parse(readFileSync(dumpAbs, 'utf8')), dumpName, program, helper };
}

export const liftTools = [
  defineTool({
    name: 'vm_boot_dump',
    title: 'VM boot dump — the decoded chunk without reversing its format',
    category: 'vm',
    readOnly: false,
    description: 'Decoded chunk of ANY Lua VM obfuscator (Luraph, IronBrew, Moonsec, PSU, Prometheus, custom …) without reversing its serialisation format. Finds the interpreter and its closure factory structurally (the script is cleaned first if needed), ports the whole loader 1:1 to Python with a hook at the top of the factory and runs it on the PRISM host: the loader deserialises its own payload, the hook writes the root proto, its upvalues, the environment and every helper table the factory reads as a JSON dump and ends the program before any virtualised code runs (the Python prelude has no OS / network access). Functions in the dump carry their Lua source offsets ($at). Output: outputs/<script>.vmdump.json + the program <script>.boot.py; run:false only writes the program (for the user to run). Feed the dump to vm_lift or chunk_disasm.',
    input: { ...SRC, run: z.boolean().optional().describe('run the program now on the PRISM host (default true; needs python3)'), ...BOOT_IN, ...OUT },
    run: async (a, ctx) => {
      const s = getSource(a, ctx);
      const base = baseName(ctx, s.scriptId);
      const v = vmSource(ctx, s.src, base, s.scriptId);
      if (!v.ok) return { text: NO_VM, data: { ok: false } };
      const b = await bootDump(ctx, v.src, base, a);
      const sid = v.scriptId ? `script_id:"${v.scriptId}", ` : '';
      const text = [`# vm_boot_dump — ${s.label}`, ...(v.line ? [v.line] : []), ...b.lines,
        ...(b.ok ? ['', 'next:', `- vm_lift {${sid}dump:"${b.dumpName}"} — devirtualised Lua for every proto`, `- chunk_disasm {${sid}chunk_output:"${b.dumpName}"} — proto layout + raw disassembly`] : [])].join('\n');
      return { text, data: { ok: b.ok, dump: b.dumpName, program: b.program, script_id: v.scriptId, helper: b.helper } };
    },
  }),
  defineTool({
    name: 'vm_lift',
    title: 'VM lift — devirtualise a VM-obfuscated script (one click)',
    category: 'vm',
    readOnly: false,
    description: 'Universal devirtualiser for Lua VM obfuscators (nothing obfuscator- or sample-specific): cleans the script if needed, gets the decoded chunk (vm_boot_dump now, or the dump you give), resolves the helper table automatically (library functions; pure wrapper slots like function(n,t,i) return unpack(t,i,n) end are inlined), specialises the interpreter on every proto — self-modifying bytecode patch discovery, constant pools, register / upvalue promotion, record folding, unflattening — and saves the lifted, structured Lua as a new workspace script. Returns the per-proto table, the notes of every pass and next steps.',
    input: {
      ...SRC,
      dump: z.string().optional().describe('dump JSON: workspace output name or file path (default: vm_boot_dump runs now)'),
      helper: z.string().optional().describe("helper table Lua name (default: auto — the factory's most called-through upvalue table)"),
      helper_path: z.string().optional().describe('path of the helper table inside the dump (default: its Lua name)'),
      only: z.array(z.string()).optional().describe('lift only these proto ids (see the table of a full run)'),
      rewrites: z.array(z.object({ from: z.string(), to: z.string() })).optional().describe('extra expression rewrite rules (metavariables __name)'),
      patch_rounds: z.number().int().min(0).max(20).optional().describe('self-modifying bytecode discovery rounds (default 6)'),
      save_script_as: z.string().optional().describe('lifted script name (default <script>.lifted.lua)'),
      ...BOOT_IN,
      ...OUT,
    },
    run: async (a, ctx) => {
      const t0 = Date.now();
      const s = getSource(a, ctx);
      const base = baseName(ctx, s.scriptId);
      const v = vmSource(ctx, s.src, base, s.scriptId);
      if (!v.ok) return { text: NO_VM, data: { ok: false } };
      const lines = [`# vm_lift — ${s.label}`, ...(v.line ? [v.line] : [])];
      let helper = a.helper ? { name: a.helper, path: a.helper_path ?? a.helper } : undefined;
      let dump: unknown;
      if (a.dump) {
        dump = JSON.parse(existsSync(a.dump) ? readFileSync(a.dump, 'utf8') : ctx.ws.readOutput(a.dump).toString('utf8'));
        lines.push(`dump: ${a.dump}`);
        if (!helper) helper = vmFactoryInfo(parse(v.src).chunk).info?.helper;
      } else {
        const b = await bootDump(ctx, v.src, base, a);
        lines.push(...b.lines);
        if (!b.ok) return { text: lines.join('\n'), data: { ok: false, program: b.program } };
        dump = b.dump;
        helper ??= b.helper;
      }
      const wr = helper ? helperWrapperRules(v.src, dump, helper) : { rules: [], notes: [] };
      const r = vmSpecialize(v.src, dump, { helper, only: a.only, rewrites: [...wr.rules, ...(a.rewrites ?? [])], patchRounds: a.patch_rounds });
      lines.push(...wr.notes.map(n => '# ' + n), ...r.notes.map(n => '# ' + n));
      if (!r.ok || !r.protos.length) return { text: lines.join('\n'), data: { ok: false } };
      const sv = saveDerived(ctx, a.save_script_as ?? base + '.lifted.lua', r.code, v.scriptId, 'vm_lift');
      const patches = ctx.ws.saveOutput(base + '.patches.json', JSON.stringify(r.patches));
      const rows = r.protos.map(p => [p.id, p.instrs, p.blocks, p.structured ? 'yes' : 'no', p.code.split('\n').length]);
      const id = sv.id ? `script_id:"${sv.id}"` : '…';
      lines.push('', `lifted ${r.protos.length} proto(s): ${r.code.split('\n').length} lines, ${r.code.length} chars — ${sv.line}`, `patches: ${patches} (${r.patches.length}); ${Date.now() - t0} ms`, '',
        table(rows, ['proto', 'instrs', 'blocks', 'structured', 'lines']), '', 'next:',
        `- strings {${id}} / constants {${id}} — every literal of the lifted program`,
        `- behavior_report {${id}} — what it does (calls, remotes, HTTP, files)`,
        `- get_function / xrefs {${id}} — read it; rename_symbols to name things`);
      return { text: lines.join('\n'), data: { ok: true, script_id: sv.id, protos: r.protos.map(p => ({ id: p.id, instrs: p.instrs, blocks: p.blocks, structured: p.structured })), patches, helper } };
    },
  }),
];
